//! Bounded, read-only evidence from the store's own commit clock.
use snapback4_core::{Engine, RuntimeError};
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

const SKIPPED_PREVIEW: usize = 32;
const TOLERANCE_MS: i64 = 5_000;
const RECENT_COMMITS: usize = 64;
const TABLE_BYTES: usize = 4096;
const TABLE_NAMES: usize = 8;
const REPORT_ERROR_BYTES: usize = 1024;
// Reserve one MiB for the outer clock/work envelope inside the host encoder.
// The reply retains `schedules` and its fired/held partition.
const REPORT_BYTE_BUDGET: usize = (crate::serve::JSON_RESPONSE_CEILING - (1 << 20)) / 2;

// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12 — inspect a fixed recent commit window, never application row values.
pub fn ahead(engine: &Engine, now: i64) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError> {
    // Reverse primary-key traversal: no full scan, sort, row payloads or retained
    // historical stamp set. octet_length(column) uses SQLite record metadata;
    // unlike a text length/cast/substr, it need not load oversized payloads.
    let mut lead = 0;
    let mut tables = BTreeSet::new();
    let mut omitted = false;
    engine.store().visit_recent_commit_clock(now.saturating_add(TOLERANCE_MS), TABLE_BYTES as i64, RECENT_COMMITS as i64, |record| {
        let at = record.at;
        if at <= now.saturating_add(TOLERANCE_MS) { return Ok(()); }
        lead = lead.max(at.saturating_sub(now));
        let length = record.length.unwrap();
        if length > TABLE_BYTES as i64 { omitted = true; return Ok(()); }
        let bytes = record.touched.unwrap();
        match serde_json::from_slice::<Vec<String>>(&bytes) {
            Ok(names) => for name in names {
                if tables.contains(&name) { continue; }
                if tables.len() < TABLE_NAMES && name.len() <= 128 { tables.insert(name); }
                else { omitted = true; }
            },
            Err(_) => omitted = true,
        }
        Ok(())
    })?;
    if lead == 0 { return Ok(None); }
    let mut names = tables.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
    if omitted { names.push("additional tables omitted".into()); }
    if names.is_empty() { names.push("no table names recorded".into()); }
    Ok(Some(format!(
        "N_CLOCK_STORE_AHEAD: recent commit stamps lead the current clock by up to {lead}ms (latest {RECENT_COMMITS} commits; tables: {}); use a fresh store per offset test ({}), or restart with the same --clock-offset (or dev --resume-clock) to continue",
        names.join(", "), crate::dev_clock::isolated_command())))
}

/// UTC calendar text for Unix milliseconds: schedule boundaries are UTC.
pub fn utc(ms: i64) -> String {
    let (days, rem) = (ms.div_euclid(86_400_000), ms.rem_euclid(86_400_000));
    // Civil-from-days (proleptic Gregorian), exact for the I53 range.
    let z = days + 719_468;
    let era = z.div_euclid(146_097);
    let doe = z - era * 146_097;
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1_460 + doe / 36_524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
    let day = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;
    let month = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 };
    let year = yoe + era * 400 + i64::from(month <= 2);
    format!("{year:04}-{month:02}-{day:02}T{:02}:{:02}:{:02}Z", rem / 3_600_000, rem % 3_600_000 / 60_000, rem % 60_000 / 1_000)
}

/// A positive duration in the units `clock advance` accepts, rounded up to a second.
pub fn span(ms: i64) -> String {
    let seconds = (ms.max(0) + 999) / 1_000;
    let (d, h, m, s) = (seconds / 86_400, seconds % 86_400 / 3_600, seconds % 3_600 / 60, seconds % 60);
    let parts: Vec<String> = [(d, "d"), (h, "h"), (m, "m"), (s, "s")].into_iter().filter(|(n, _)| *n > 0).map(|(n, unit)| format!("{n}{unit}")).collect();
    if parts.is_empty() { "0s".into() } else { parts.join("") }
}

/// Each schedule's saved boundary, in declaration order.
pub fn saved_boundaries(engine: &Engine) -> Vec<Option<i64>> {
    engine.schema().schedules.iter()
        .map(|schedule| {
            let shape = engine.store().schedule_shape(&schedule.name).ok().flatten();
            if shape.as_ref().is_some_and(|shape| *shape != snapback4_core::value::digest(schedule)) { return None; }
            engine.store().schedule_boundary(&schedule.name).ok().flatten()
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Preflight is bounded before the clock or worker leases change.
// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12.1 — only explicit execution enumerates all crossed windows; coalesced reports keep a bounded preview.
pub fn crossed_boundaries(engine: &Engine, before: &[Option<i64>], now: i64, held: bool, each_boundary: bool) -> Result<Vec<(usize, i64)>, snapback4_core::Refusal> {
    let mut boundaries = Vec::new();
    let mut report_bytes = 0usize;
    for (index, schedule) in engine.schema().schedules.iter().enumerate() {
        // JSON may escape every error byte; count that bound per schedule.
        report_bytes = report_bytes.saturating_add(2048 + 6 * (REPORT_ERROR_BYTES + 3) + 8 * (schedule.name.len() + schedule.target.len()));
        if report_bytes > REPORT_BYTE_BUDGET { return Err(crate::dev_clock::input("schedule report exceeds its byte budget; reduce the declared schedules")); }
        if held { continue; }
        let Some(old) = before.get(index).copied().flatten() else { continue; };
        let end = schedule.boundary(now);
        if old >= end { continue; }
        let periods = schedule.periods_between(old, end);
        if each_boundary && periods > (10_000 - boundaries.len()) as i64 {
            return Err(crate::dev_clock::input("--each-boundary crosses more than 10000 schedule windows; use a smaller duration or omit --each-boundary to coalesce"));
        }
        report_bytes = report_bytes.saturating_add((if each_boundary { periods as usize } else { (periods as usize).min(SKIPPED_PREVIEW + 1) }).saturating_mul(1024 + 8 * schedule.target.len()));
        if report_bytes > REPORT_BYTE_BUDGET { return Err(crate::dev_clock::input("schedule window report exceeds its byte budget; use a smaller duration")); }
        if !each_boundary { continue; }
        let mut boundary = schedule.next(old);
        while boundary <= end {
            boundaries.push((index, boundary));
            boundary = schedule.next(boundary);
        }
    }
    boundaries.sort_by_key(|(index, at)| (*at, *index));
    Ok(boundaries)
}

fn period(schedule: &snapback4_core::schema::Schedule) -> String {
    schedule.describe()
}

/// What each schedule did on one clock advance, and why one did not fire.
/// The core fires each schedule at most once per advance, for the latest
/// boundary, and holds it while its saved boundary is ahead of the clock.
// @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — missed boundaries fire once; this only explains them.
pub fn schedule_report(engine: &Engine, before: &[Option<i64>], fired: &[String], now: i64, held: bool, each_boundary: bool, port: Option<u16>) -> Vec<serde_json::Value> {
    let after = saved_boundaries(engine);
    // Read only bounded summaries: job args/cursors and full error payloads
    // are irrelevant to this report and must not be loaded then replicated.
    let runs = job_summaries(engine).unwrap_or_default();
    engine.schema().schedules.iter().enumerate().map(|(index, schedule)| {
        let (old, saved) = (before.get(index).copied().flatten(), after.get(index).copied().flatten());
        let current = schedule.boundary(now);
        let next = schedule.next(current);
        let mut entry = serde_json::json!({ "name": schedule.name, "target": schedule.target, "period": period(schedule), "fired": false, "firedWindows": [], "skippedBoundaries": [], "nextBoundary": utc(next) });
        if fired.contains(&schedule.name) {
            let end = saved.unwrap_or(current);
            entry["fired"] = true.into();
            let start = schedule.previous(end);
            let window = |boundary| serde_json::json!({"periodStart": schedule.previous(boundary), "periodEnd": boundary});
            let mut windows = Vec::new();
            if each_boundary {
                if let Some(old) = old {
                    let mut at = schedule.next(old);
                    while at <= end { windows.push(window(at)); at = schedule.next(at); }
                }
            } else { windows.push(window(end)); }
            if each_boundary {
                entry["reason"] = format!("fired {} windows: {}", windows.len(), windows.iter().map(|window| format!("{} to {}", utc(window["periodStart"].as_i64().unwrap()), utc(window["periodEnd"].as_i64().unwrap()))).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("; ")).into();
            }
            entry["firedWindows"] = windows.into();
            entry["periodStart"] = start.into();
            entry["periodEnd"] = end.into();
            if !each_boundary { entry["reason"] = format!("fired for the period {} to {}", utc(start), utc(end)).into(); }
            if let Some(run) = runs.get(&schedule.target) { entry["run"] = run.clone(); }
            // @ref LLP 3000.040#24-monthly-and-yearly-schedules — calendar periods count boundaries, not milliseconds.
            let skipped = if each_boundary { 0 } else { old.map(|old| schedule.periods_between(old, end) - 1).unwrap_or(0) };
            if skipped > 0 {
                entry["skippedPeriods"] = skipped.into();
                let mut windows = Vec::new();
                let mut at = schedule.next(old.unwrap());
                while at < end && windows.len() < SKIPPED_PREVIEW {
                    let mut item = window(at);
                    let mut args = serde_json::Map::new();
                    if let Some(program) = engine.program(&schedule.target) {
                        if program.args.contains_key("periodStart") { args.insert("periodStart".into(), schedule.previous(at).into()); }
                        if program.args.contains_key("periodEnd") { args.insert("periodEnd".into(), at.into()); }
                    }
                    item["command"] = format!("snapback4 run {} '{}'{}", schedule.target, serde_json::Value::Object(args), port.map(|port| format!(" --port {port}")).unwrap_or_default()).into();
                    windows.push(item); at = schedule.next(at);
                }
                entry["skippedBoundariesOmitted"] = (skipped - windows.len() as i64).into();
                entry["skippedBoundaries"] = windows.into();
                entry["reason"] = format!("fired once, for the latest period {} to {}; {skipped} earlier period{} this advance crossed (from {}) did not run: missed boundaries fire once. Run {} with periodStart/periodEnd for an earlier period",
                    utc(start), utc(end), if skipped == 1 { "" } else { "s" }, utc(old.unwrap_or(end)), schedule.target).into();
            }
        } else if held {
            entry["holdCode"] = "disabled".into();
            entry["reason"] = "schedules are held (dev --hold-schedules or --replay); a restart without the flag resumes at the next boundary".into();
        } else if let Some(saved) = saved.filter(|saved| old.is_some() && *saved >= current) {
            let due = schedule.next(saved);
            entry["holdCode"] = "saved-boundary".into();
            entry["savedBoundary"] = saved.into();
            entry["heldUntil"] = utc(due).into();
            entry["nextBoundary"] = utc(due).into();
            entry["reason"] = format!("held by the store: boundary {} was already processed and this clock {} has not reached its next window (restarting resets the process offset, not the saved boundary). One fire per boundary. Advance {} more, or use a fresh staging deployment/store for an independent test; keep the same --clock-offset when continuing a test across serve restarts",
                utc(saved), utc(now), span(due - now)).into();
        } else if old != saved {
            entry["holdCode"] = "initialized".into();
            entry["reason"] = format!("{} started at boundary {}: a schedule fires at the boundary after the first one it sees, next {} ({} from now)",
                if old.is_none() { "this schedule" } else { "this changed schedule" }, utc(saved.unwrap_or(current)), utc(next), span(next - now)).into();
        } else {
            entry["holdCode"] = "not-due".into();
            entry["reason"] = format!("next boundary {} ({} from now; schedule times are UTC)", utc(next), span(next - now)).into();
        }
        entry
    }).collect()
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#10-wave-20-loop-repairs-dx5 — every declared schedule has one reported outcome.
pub fn outcomes(schedules: &[serde_json::Value]) -> (Vec<serde_json::Value>, Vec<serde_json::Value>) {
    schedules.iter().cloned().partition(|schedule| schedule["fired"] == true)
}

/// The report never loads full error/argument payloads from retained jobs.
fn job_summaries(engine: &Engine) -> Result<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>, RuntimeError> {
    let mut summaries = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
    for summary in engine.store().job_summaries(REPORT_ERROR_BYTES)? {
        let name = summary.name;
        if summaries.contains_key(&name) { continue; }
        let mut error = summary.error;
        let truncated = summary.error_truncated;
        if let Some(text) = &mut error && truncated {
            let mut end = REPORT_ERROR_BYTES.min(text.len());
            while !text.is_char_boundary(end) { end -= 1; }
            text.truncate(end); text.push('…');
        }
        summaries.insert(name, serde_json::json!({ "id":summary.id, "state":summary.state,
            "rowsWritten":summary.rows_written, "error":error, "errorTruncated":truncated }));
    }
    Ok(summaries)
}

/// Startup lines for schedules the store holds: their saved boundary leads the clock.
pub fn held_schedules(engine: &Engine, now: i64) -> Vec<String> {
    engine.schema().schedules.iter().zip(saved_boundaries(engine)).filter_map(|(schedule, saved)| {
        let saved = saved.filter(|saved| *saved > schedule.boundary(now))?;
        let due = schedule.next(saved);
        Some(format!("clock     schedule {} is held until {} ({} from now): its saved boundary {} is ahead of this clock; `clock advance {}` or restart with dev --resume-clock",
            schedule.name, utc(due), span(due - now), utc(saved), span(due - now)))
    }).collect()
}

/// The dev clock offset that continues a store's own time: its newest
/// recent commit stamp (or saved schedule boundary) less wall time, never negative.
pub fn resume_offset(store: &snapback4_core::Store, wall: i64) -> Result<i64, RuntimeError> {
    let commit = store.recent_commit_max_at(RECENT_COMMITS as i64)?;
    let boundary = store.latest_schedule_boundary()?;
    let latest = commit.into_iter().chain(boundary).max().unwrap_or(wall);
    // Whole seconds, rounded up, so restarting twice does not drift backwards.
    Ok((latest.saturating_sub(wall).max(0) + 999) / 1_000 * 1_000)
}

pub fn has_data(engine: &Engine) -> bool {
    engine.store().inspection_has_data().unwrap_or(false)
}

pub fn offset_line(offset: i64, running: bool) -> String {
    format!("clock     offset from wall time: {offset:+}ms{}", if running { " (lasts until restart)" } else { " (no running dev; inspecting against wall time)" })
}

pub(super) fn advance(request: Request, shared: &Shared, body: &str) {
    let service = match clock_service(&request, shared) {
        Ok(service) => service,
        Err(why) => return respond(request,403,json!({"denied":refusal_json(&why)})),
    };
    let payload = match serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(body) {
        Ok(payload) => payload,
        Err(_) => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&crate::dev_clock::input("clock advance takes {\"duration\":\"+2m\"}"))})),
    };
    let each_boundary = match payload.get("eachBoundary") {
        None => false,
        Some(serde_json::Value::Bool(value)) => *value,
        Some(_) => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&crate::dev_clock::input("eachBoundary must be a boolean"))})),
    };
    let duration = payload.get("duration").and_then(|value| value.as_str());
    let milliseconds = match duration.ok_or_else(|| crate::dev_clock::input("clock advance takes {\"duration\":\"+2m\"}"))
        .and_then(crate::dev_clock::duration) {
        Ok(milliseconds) => milliseconds,
        Err(error) => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error)})),
    };
    // Serialize clock callers only. Background slices check advancing after
    // engine admission and skip during this synchronous drain.
    let advance = lock(&shared.maintenance).advance.clone();
    let _advance = lock(&advance);
    let _advancing = Advancing(shared);
    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12 — simulated time makes retries due without stealing a live worker's claim or viewer session.
    let advanced = (|| {
        // Match claims' engine-then-clock lock order: no claim can land
        // between shifting its lease and publishing the advanced clock.
        let mut engine = lock(&shared.engine);
        let before = crate::dev_clock_store::saved_boundaries(&engine);
        if let Some(principal) = &service {
            if engine.store().meta("deployment_environment").map_err(|e|e.refusal())?.as_deref() != Some("staging") { return Err(crate::dev_clock::release()); }
            super::session_identity::mutation_authority(&request,shared,&engine,principal)?;
        } else { shared.dev_authority(&engine)?; }
        let mut clock = lock(&shared.clock);
        let mut next = clock.clone();
        let now = next.advance(milliseconds)?.max(shared.time_audience_clock.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire));
        let boundaries = crate::dev_clock_store::crossed_boundaries(&engine, &before, now, shared.hold_schedules, each_boundary)?;
        lock(&shared.maintenance).advancing = true;
        engine.advance_worker_leases_at(milliseconds, clock.now()).map_err(|e| e.refusal())?;
        *clock = next;
        let offset = clock.offset();
        let skew = now - snapback4_core::now_ms();
        let isolated = if crate::dev_clock_store::has_data(&engine) {
            format!("; use {} for isolated time tests; clock advance --port N targets its printed port (guide jobs)", crate::dev_clock::isolated_command())
        } else { String::new() };
        let message = format!("cumulative offset {offset:+}ms (requested process offset; now includes the authoritative floor); process offset lasts until restart{isolated}");
        Ok((now, offset, skew, message, before, boundaries))
    })();
    let (now, offset, skew, message, before, boundaries) = match advanced {
        Ok(result) => result,
        Err(error) => return respond(request, 400, json!({"denied":refusal_json(&error)})),
    };
    // @ref LLP 3000#contended-read-serving — a developer is awaiting this
    // request; synchronous clock-advance work intentionally keeps request QoS.
    let drained = (|| {
        let mut crossed = Vec::new();
        if each_boundary {
            for (index, at) in boundaries {
                crossed.extend(engine_work(shared, |engine, _| engine.fire_schedule_boundary_at(shared.now(), index, at))?);
            }
        }
        let mut work = work_at(shared, true, 0, Some(now))?;
        work.schedules += crossed.len();
        work.fired.extend(crossed);
        Ok::<_, RuntimeError>(work)
    })();
    match drained.map_err(|error| error.refusal()).and_then(|work| completed_drain(work, crate::lifecycle::stopping())) {
        Ok(work) => {
            let schedules = crate::dev_clock_store::schedule_report(&lock(&shared.engine), &before, &work.fired, now, shared.hold_schedules, each_boundary, shared.dev_identity.as_ref().map(|i| i.address.port()));
            let (fired, held) = crate::dev_clock_store::outcomes(&schedules);
            respond(request, 200, json!({"now":now, "advancedMs":milliseconds, "sessionNotice":crate::dev_clock::SESSION_NOTICE, "offsetMs":offset, "skewMs":skew, "eachBoundary":each_boundary, "message":message, "work":work, "schedules":schedules, "fired":fired, "held":held}))
        }
        // Time remains advanced if maintenance fails; callers must not
        // retry the advance blindly. The normal tick retries pending work.
        Err(error) => respond(request, 500, json!({"now":now, "advancedMs":milliseconds, "sessionNotice":crate::dev_clock::SESSION_NOTICE, "offsetMs":offset, "skewMs":skew, "eachBoundary":each_boundary, "message":message, "denied":refusal_json(&error)})),
    }
}

    };

        Ok(payload) => payload,
        Err(error) => return refuse(request, 400, Refusal::new("E_INPUT", "input", format!("the request body is not JSON: {error}; send {{\"args\":{{..}}}}"))),
    };
    if service_route && !shared.personas {crate::release_requests::Scope::admit(&shared.release_requests,||*lock(&shared.generation));}
    let program = lock(&shared.bound).programs.iter().find(|p| p.program.name == name).map(|p| p.program.clone());
    let program = match program {

        Some(other) => return refuse(request, 404, Refusal::new("E_OP", "op", format!("{name} is a {}, not a job; queries are POST /q/<op>, mutations POST /m/<op>", other.kind.word()))),
//! A process-local clock for development and explicitly classified staging stores.
use snapback4_core::error::Refusal;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#8-wave-18-developer-loop-amendment-dx4 — preserve expiry tests and tell callers how to recover.
pub(crate) const SESSION_NOTICE: &str = "Time travel also advances session expiry and unplaced-upload collection: seven-day password sessions may now be expired. Sign in again after the jump and upload unplaced bytes after it; never replay an ambiguous clock advance.";

const MAX_TIME: i64 = snapback4_core::value::I53_MAX;

pub fn input(message: impl Into<String>) -> Refusal { Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_INPUT", "clock", message).guide("clock") }
pub fn release() -> Refusal { Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY", "clock", "clock controls require dev or a deploy --staging store; production always uses wall time").guide("clock") }

/// Isolated time tests stay inside an assigned range, or request a free port.
pub(crate) fn isolated_command() -> String {
    isolated_range(std::env::var("PORT_LO").ok().as_deref(), std::env::var("PORT_HI").ok().as_deref())
}
fn isolated_range(lo: Option<&str>, hi: Option<&str>) -> String {
    match (lo.and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok()), hi.and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok())) {
        (Some(lo), Some(hi)) if lo > 0 && hi >= lo => format!("dev --memory --port {lo}-{hi} within the current range"),
        _ => "dev --memory --port 0".into(),
    }
}

pub fn duration(text: &str) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    if text.starts_with('-') { return Err(input("clock advance cannot move backwards; use a positive duration such as +2m")); }
    let text = text.strip_prefix('+').unwrap_or(text);
    let split = text.bytes().position(|b| !b.is_ascii_digit()).unwrap_or(text.len());
    let (number, unit) = text.split_at(split);
    let multiplier = match unit { "ms" => 1, "s" => 1_000, "m" => 60_000, "h" => 3_600_000, "d" => 86_400_000, "w" => 604_800_000, _ => 0 };
    number.parse::<i64>().ok().and_then(|n| n.checked_mul(multiplier)).filter(|n| *n > 0 && *n <= MAX_TIME)
        .ok_or_else(|| input("expected a positive whole duration with ms, s, m, h, d or w, such as +25h"))
}

pub fn offset(text: &str) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    if let Some(rest) = text.strip_prefix('-') { duration(rest).map(|n| -n) } else { duration(text) }
}

fn time(value: Option<i64>) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    value.filter(|n| (0..=MAX_TIME).contains(n)).ok_or_else(|| input("time must be Unix milliseconds in 0..9007199254740991; choose a smaller time or duration"))
}

pub fn run_now(text: Option<&String>) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    let now = snapback4_core::now_ms();
    match text {
        None => Ok(now),
        Some(text) if text.starts_with('+') => time(now.checked_add(duration(text)?)),
        Some(text) => time(text.parse().ok()),
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Clock {
    dev: bool,
    base: i64,
    offset: i64,
    started: Instant,
    epoch: String,
    revision: u64,
    #[cfg(test)]
    frozen: bool,
}

impl Clock {
    pub fn new(dev: bool, offset: i64) -> Result<Self, Refusal> {
        if !dev && offset != 0 { return Err(release()); }
        Ok(Self { dev, offset, base: time(snapback4_core::now_ms().checked_add(offset))?, started: Instant::now(),
            epoch: snapback4_core::ids::mint(snapback4_core::now_ms(), &mut snapback4_core::ids::Mint::default()).map_err(|e| e.refusal())?, revision: 0, #[cfg(test)] frozen: false })
    }
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(crate) fn freeze(&mut self, now: i64) { self.base = now; self.frozen = true; }
    pub fn now(&self) -> i64 {
        #[cfg(test)] if self.frozen { return self.base; }
        if !self.dev { return snapback4_core::now_ms(); }
        self.base.saturating_add(self.started.elapsed().as_millis().min(MAX_TIME as u128) as i64).min(MAX_TIME)
    }
    /// Identifies samples taken before/after a restart or deliberate clock jump.
    pub fn offset(&self) -> i64 { self.offset }
    pub fn revision(&self) -> String { format!("{}:{}", self.epoch, self.revision) }
    pub fn presence_now(&self) -> i64 {
        // Production grace is elapsed real time, unaffected by wall-clock corrections.
        if self.dev { self.now() } else { self.started.elapsed().as_millis().min(MAX_TIME as u128) as i64 }
    }
    /// Back to wall time: the offset `--clock-offset` and every advance added
    /// is dropped (a development reset's `{"clock":"reset"}`).
    pub fn reset(&mut self) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
        if !self.dev { return Err(release()); }
        self.revision += 1;
        self.offset = 0;
        self.base = snapback4_core::now_ms();
        self.started = Instant::now();
        #[cfg(test)] { self.frozen = false; }
        Ok(self.base)
    }
    pub fn advance(&mut self, milliseconds: i64) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
        if !self.dev { return Err(release()); }
        if milliseconds <= 0 { return Err(input("clock advance cannot move backwards; use a positive duration such as +2m")); }
        let next = time(self.now().checked_add(milliseconds))?;
        let offset = self.offset.checked_add(milliseconds).ok_or_else(|| input("cumulative clock offset overflow"))?;
        self.revision += 1;
        self.offset = offset;
        self.base = next;
        self.started = Instant::now();
        Ok(next)
    }
}

/// The control CLI only talks to a loopback dev host. It does not open its store.
pub fn command(options: &crate::verbs::Options) -> i32 {
    let result = (|| -> Result<String, String> {
        if options.positionals.len() != 2 || options.positionals[0] != "advance" {
            return Err(input(format!("usage: {}", crate::cli_flags::synopsis("clock"))).to_string());
        }
        duration(&options.positionals[1]).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let release_path = options.flags.get("release").map(|dir| std::path::PathBuf::from(dir).join("store.sqlite"));
        if release_path.is_some() && options.flags.contains_key("port") { return Err("clock --release does not accept --port".into()); }
        let (address, instance, token) = if let Some(path) = &release_path {
            let store = snapback4_core::Store::open_read_only(path).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            if store.meta("deployment_environment").map_err(|e|e.to_string())?.as_deref() != Some("staging") { return Err(release().to_string()); }
            let address = crate::store_owner::inspector_address(path).ok_or("staging clock requires a running serve")?;
            let session = crate::serve::token::mint_live(path, "clock", 1).map_err(|(_,error)|error)?;
            (address,None,Some(session.token))
        } else { let (address,instance)=crate::verbs::dev_address(options)?; (address,instance,None) };
        let body = serde_json::json!({"duration":options.positionals[1],"eachBoundary":options.flags.contains_key("each-boundary")}).to_string();
        // The common HTTP/1.0 exchange is EOF-delimited and bounds replies at
        // 64 MiB, enough for the preflight's complete explicit window report.
        let response = if let Some(token) = &token {
            crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange_authorized(address,"POST","/dev/clock/advance",None,Some(token),&body,Duration::from_secs(60))
        } else { crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange_dev(address, "/dev/clock/advance", instance.as_deref(), &body, Duration::from_secs(60)) };
        let (status, json) = response.map_err(|error| {
            let evidence = crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange(address, "GET", "/dev/status", None, "", Duration::from_secs(5)).ok()
                .map(|(_, status)| format!("now={}, skewMs={}", status["now"], status["skewMs"]))
                .unwrap_or_else(|| "clock status unavailable".into());
            format!("clock advance reply failed at {address}: {error}; time may already have advanced ({evidence}); inspect /dev/status and queued work before retrying; for an isolated dev pass --port N")
        })?;
        if let Some(notice) = json["sessionNotice"].as_str() { eprintln!("clock: {notice}"); }
        if let Some(held) = json["held"].as_array() {
            for schedule in held.iter().filter(|s| s["holdCode"] == "saved-boundary") {
                eprintln!("clock: schedule {}: {}", schedule["name"].as_str().unwrap_or("?"), schedule["reason"].as_str().unwrap_or("held"));
            }
        }
        if let Some(denied) = json.get("denied") {
            let clock = json["message"].as_str().map(|message| format!("; time remains advanced: {message}")).unwrap_or_default();
            return Err(format!("{}: {}{clock}\n  guide: clock", denied["code"].as_str().unwrap_or("E_CLOCK_INPUT"), denied["message"].as_str().unwrap_or("clock advance failed")));
        }
        if status != 200 { return Err(format!("dev refused clock advance: {json}")); }
        Ok(json.to_string())
    })();
    match result { Ok(body) => { println!("{body}"); 0 }, Err(error) => { eprintln!("{error}"); 1 } }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod isolated_tests {
    #[test]
    fn time_test_guidance_uses_only_valid_assigned_ranges_or_a_free_port() {
        assert_eq!(super::isolated_range(Some("24000"), Some("24009")), "dev --memory --port 24000-24009 within the current range");

            assert_eq!(super::isolated_range(lo,hi), "dev --memory --port 0");
        }
    }

//! Query result paths and nullable reads of private side tables.
use super::*;

pub(super) const VIEWER_KEY: &str = "$lookupViewerKey";
const TARGET_ROW: &str = "$lookupTargetRow";

// @ref LLP 3000.036.002#151-evidence-and-decision — compatibility keeps
// fallthrough null; check must name a concrete uncovered source path.
pub(super) fn fallthrough(decl: &ast::ProgramDecl) -> Diagnostic {
    fn path(body: &[S], implicit: bool) -> Option<Vec<String>> {
        let mut route = Vec::new();
        for (at, stmt) in body.iter().enumerate() {
            match stmt {
                S::Return { .. } => return None,
                S::Expr { .. } if implicit && at + 1 == body.len() => return None,
                S::Require { condition: A::Literal { value: Literal::Bool(false), .. }, .. } => return None,
                S::If { then_body, else_body, site, .. } => {
                    let completes = implicit && at + 1 == body.len();
                    let (arm, rest) = if let Some(rest) = path(then_body, completes) { ("true", rest) }
                        else if let Some(rest) = path(else_body, completes) { ("false", rest) }
                        else { return None };
                    route.push(format!("if at {site} is {arm}")); route.extend(rest);
                }
                S::For { site, .. } => route.push(format!("loop at {site} has zero iterations")),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Some(route)
    }
    let route = path(&decl.body, true).unwrap_or_default();
    let route = if route.is_empty() { "entry → end".into() } else { format!("{} → end", route.join(" → ")) };
    Diagnostic::new(&decl.site, "N_QUERY_FALLTHROUGH",
        format!("query {} can finish without a result ({route}); that path returns null", decl.name),
        "return a value on this path: add `return []` for an intentionally empty list, or `return null` for intentional absence; a return inside a possibly empty loop does not cover its zero-iteration path").guide("programs")
}

impl Binder<'_> {
    fn lookup_rule_proved(&self, value: &A) -> bool {
        let mut copy = value.clone();
        let mut target = false;
        super::super::intent_walk::expression(&mut copy, &mut |node| {
            if matches!(node, A::Name { name, .. } if name == TARGET_ROW) { target = true; }
        });
        if !target { return self.point_guard_safe(value) && self.authorization_proved(value, true); }
        match value {
            A::Binary { op, left, right, .. } if op == "or" => self.lookup_rule_proved(left) || self.lookup_rule_proved(right),
            A::Binary { op, left, right, .. } if op == "and" => self.lookup_rule_proved(left) && self.lookup_rule_proved(right),
            _ => false,
        }
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#152-lookup-contract-and-diagnostics — transport
    // only source advice facts across the helper's captured argument boundary.
    pub(super) fn helper_lookup_points(&self, function: &ast::FunctionDecl, args: &[A]) -> Vec<ReadExpr> {
        fn closed(value: &A, parameters: &[ast::ArgDecl]) -> bool {
            let mut value = value.clone();
            let mut safe = true;
            super::super::intent_walk::expression(&mut value, &mut |node| match node {
                A::Name { name, .. } if name != "viewer" && name != "now" && !parameters.iter().any(|p| p.name == *name) => safe = false,
                A::Focal { .. } | A::Write { .. } | A::Call { .. } => safe = false,
                _ => {}
            });
            safe
        }
        fn substitute(value: &mut A, parameters: &[ast::ArgDecl], args: &[A]) {
            super::super::intent_walk::expression(value, &mut |node| {
                if let A::Name { name, .. } = node && let Some(at) = parameters.iter().position(|p| p.name == *name)
                    && let Some(argument) = args.get(at) { *node = argument.clone(); }
            });
        }
        fn collect(catalog: &Catalog, function: &ast::FunctionDecl, args: &[A], stack: &mut Vec<String>, fuel: &mut usize, reads: &mut Vec<ReadExpr>) {
            if stack.len() >= 32 || stack.contains(&function.name) { return; }
            stack.push(function.name.clone());
            let mut body = match &function.body { ast::FunctionBody::Block(body) => body.clone(), ast::FunctionBody::Expression(value) => vec![S::Return { value: value.clone(), site: value.site().clone() }] };
            super::super::intent_walk::statements(&mut body, &mut |node| {
                if *fuel == 0 { return; } *fuel -= 1;
                match node {
                    A::Read(read) if read.keys.iter().all(|key| closed(&key.value, &function.args)) => {
                        let mut value = A::Read(read.clone()); substitute(&mut value, &function.args, args);
                        if let A::Read(read) = value { reads.push(read); }
                    }
                    A::Call { name, args: arguments, .. } if arguments.iter().all(|value| closed(value, &function.args)) => {
                        if let Some(callee) = catalog.functions.get(name) {
                            let mut arguments = arguments.clone();
                            for value in &mut arguments { substitute(value, &function.args, args); }
                            collect(catalog, callee, &arguments, stack, fuel, reads);
                        }
                    }
                    _ => {}
                }
            });
            stack.pop();
        }
        if self.caller_kind != ProgramKind::Mutation { return Vec::new(); }
        let identity: Vec<_> = function.args.iter().map(|p| A::Name { name: p.name.clone(), site: p.site.clone() }).collect();
        let mut reads = Vec::new();
        collect(self.catalog, function, &identity, &mut Vec::new(), &mut 512, &mut reads);
        reads.into_iter().filter(|read| read.keys.iter().all(|key| closed(&key.value, &function.args))).filter(|read| {
            let mut value = A::Read(read.clone()); substitute(&mut value, &function.args, args);
            let A::Read(actual) = value else { return false };
            self.point_guard_safe(&A::Read(actual.clone())) && (self.point_present(&actual) || self.lookup_point_present(&actual) || self.row_independent_read_proved(&actual.table))
        }).collect()
    }
    // This marker suppresses advice only; it cannot authorize a runtime read
    // or enter the binder's authority/presence proof domains.
    pub(super) fn lookup_viewer_key(&self, value: &A) -> bool {
        if matches!(value, A::Name { name, .. } if name == "viewer" || self.binding(name)
            .is_some_and(|binding| binding.fields.contains_key(&vec![VIEWER_KEY.into()]))) { return true; }
        let equal = A::Binary { op: "=".into(), left: Box::new(value.clone()), right: Box::new(A::Name { name: "viewer".into(), site: value.site().clone() }), site: value.site().clone() };
        self.point_guard_safe(value) && self.authorization_proved(&equal, true)
    }

// @ref LLP 3000.031#3 — named arms preserve generic covariance.
// Every arm retains T; absent additionally proves null or an empty array.
interface Present<out T> extends ReadyMetadata {
  readonly existence: "present";
  readonly data: T & ({} | undefined);
}
interface Partial<out T> extends ReadyMetadata {
  readonly existence: "partial";
  readonly data: T;
}
interface Absent<out T> extends ReadyMetadata {
  readonly existence: "absent";
  readonly data: T & (null | []);
  readonly complete: true;
  readonly cut: null;
}
export type Ready<T> = Present<T> | Partial<T> | Absent<T>;
export type Read<T> =
  | Ready<T>
  | { readonly loading: true }
  | { readonly denied: Refusal };
/** A one-shot's final answer; ready can still be partial or stale. */
export type SettledRead<T> = Exclude<Read<T>, { readonly loading: true }>;

/** Engine work for this server answer under dev; never returned by serve. */
export interface ReadMeter {
  /** Precise reason, including non-uniform work that public `Read.cut` withholds. */
  readonly cut: ReadCut;
  readonly examined: number;
  readonly indexEntries: number;
  readonly probes: number;
  readonly steps: number;
  readonly heapBytes: number;
  readonly outputBytes: number;
  readonly rowsWritten: number;
}

/** List matching keeps denial explicit; otherwise also handles uncertain lists.
 * Named partial/loading/absent/present handlers always win. */
export type ReadMatchListHandlers<T extends readonly unknown[], R = unknown> =
  Pick<ReadMatchHandlers<T, R>, "denied"> & {
    [K in "loading" | "absent" | "partial" | "present"]?: ReadMatchHandlers<T, R>[K];
  } & { otherwise: (read: Read<T>) => R };

// @ref LLP 3000.031#9-wave-12-list-matching — explicit list fallback covers partial without erasing denial.
export function matchReadList<T extends readonly unknown[], H extends NoInfer<ReadMatchListHandlers<T>>>(
  input: Matchable<T>, handlers: H,
): ReturnType<Extract<H[keyof H], (...args: never[]) => unknown>>;
export function matchReadList<T extends readonly unknown[], R>(input: Matchable<T>, handlers: ReadMatchListHandlers<T, R>): R {
  const read: Read<T> = "loadMore" in input && "read" in input ? input.read : input as Read<T>;
  if ("denied" in read && typeof handlers.denied !== "function") throw new TypeError("matchReadList: denial is mandatory; add denied: why => …");
  return matchRead(read, { ...handlers, partial: handlers.partial ?? ((_data, current) => handlers.otherwise(current)) });
}

/** The fallback `otherwiseAll` builds: marked, so `matchRead` also sends the
 * denied and partial states the call does not name to it. The mark is a plain

    pub(in crate::engine) fn upsert_absence_proven(&mut self, table: &str, index: &str, key: &[Value]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
        let expressions: Vec<_> = key.iter().map(|value| {
            if *value == Value::Id(self.context.viewer.clone()) { Expr::Input(Input::Viewer) } else { Expr::Literal(value.clone()) }
        }).collect();
        let Ok(visibility) = crate::engine::rules::upsert_absence(self.schema, table, index, &expressions) else { return Ok(false) };
        if self.retained_group(table, index, key)? { return Ok(false); }
        if visibility.decided_true { return Ok(true); }
        // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.5 — the parent key decides authorization; the child's acquired partition separately proves absence.
        let definition = &self.schema.tables[table];
        let rule = definition.rules.read.device_audience_rule().into_owned();
        if let Some(through) = &definition.through
            && !rule.is_uniformly_readable()
            && let Some(id) = definition.index(index).expect("checked index").columns().iter().zip(key).find_map(|(column, value)| (column == &through.reference).then_some(value))
        {
            let verdict = self.device_work(|runner| runner.parent_verdict(table, through, id))?;
            return Ok(verdict == crate::engine::through::ParentVerdict::Readable && !self.beyond_horizon);
        }
        // A uniform key can still name somebody else's private group. Evaluate
        // the rule over only its pinned columns, never using trust_synced_read:
        // the synthetic row was not delivered. A positive membership witness
        // may establish readability; an unknown probe must still queue.
        let row = crate::value::Supplied::key(definition.index(index).expect("checked index"),key,&TargetInput(()));
        let viewer = self.context.viewer.clone();
        self.meter.heap(row.heap_bytes())?;
        let readable = self.authorized_scratch(self.rule_scratch(&rule), &[(MeterKind::RuleProbes, rule_probes(&rule))], |runner, allowance| {
            crate::engine::rules::evaluate(&rule, &viewer, None, &row, false, &mut crate::engine::read::RuleProbe { runner, allowance })
        })?;
        Ok(readable && !self.beyond_horizon)
    }

            if !key.contains(&Value::Null) && !self.upsert_absence_proven(table, name, &key)? {

/** What `useQuery(op, args)` returns, named by the operation, for props:
 * `function Header({ me }: { me: UseQuery<typeof api.myProfile> })`. A hook
 * result is the read itself; narrow it with `matchRead` or the guards. */
// @ref LLP 3000.013#6.4 — hook results are named by the operation, like UseMutation.
export type UseQuery<O> = O extends Query<any, any> ? Read<ResultOf<O>> : never;
/** What `usePage` returns: the rows of every requested page (deduplicated by
 * row id), whether another page exists, the combined read, and `loadMore`.
 * Guards take `page.read`; `matchRead` also accepts the whole page. */
export interface PageHook<R extends readonly unknown[]> {
  items: R[number][];
  hasMore: boolean;
  read: Read<R>;
  loadMore: () => void;
}
/** What `usePage(op, args)` returns, named by the operation, for props:
 * `function More({ page }: { page: UsePage<typeof api.thread> })`. */
export type UsePage<O> = O extends Query<any, any> ? ResultOf<O> extends readonly unknown[] ? PageHook<ResultOf<O>> : never : never;

    fn collision_lookup(&mut self, table: &str, name: &str, index: &crate::schema::Index, key: &[Value], except: Option<&str>, effect: Effect) -> Result<Option<Value>, RuntimeError> {
        let probes = super::rules::rule_probes(&self.schema.tables[table].rules.read);
        self.authorized_scan(&[(MeterKind::RuleProbes, probes)], |runner, allowance| {
            let found = if runner.schema.tables[table].not_before.is_some() {
                runner.lookup_write_occupant(table, name, index, key)?
            } else {
                runner.live_lookup(allowance, table, name, index, key, #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")] None)?
            };
            if let Some(row) = &found && Some(row.field("id")?.as_str()?) != except {
                runner.observe_sequence_columns(table, row, &index.columns(), effect == Effect::Insert)?;
                runner.visible_collision(table, row, effect, &format!("unique {}", index.columns().join(", ")))?;
            }
            Ok(found)
        })
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — hidden collisions use the ordinary write-rule refusal
    fn visible_collision(
        &mut self,
        table: &str,
        row: &Value,
        effect: Effect,
        clause: &str,
    ) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let mut image = row.clone();
        let definition = self.schema.table(table).expect("validated");
        materialize_optional_fields(&mut image, definition);
        if self.inactive_write_target(table, &image)? || !self.check_rule(table, Effect::Read, None, &image)? {
            return Err(self.rule_refusal(table, effect, clause));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

// For SVG/foreignObject controls, click the actual rendered box, not a text
// descendant whose DOM geometry Playwright may interpret differently.
async function clickSvg(page, control) {
  await control.waitFor({ state: "visible" });
  const box = await control.boundingBox();
  assert.ok(box && box.width > 0 && box.height > 0, "SVG control has no rendered box");
  await page.mouse.click(box.x + box.width / 2, box.y + box.height / 2);
}

  web = await startStatic("dist", options);
  await withBrowser({ executablePath: process.env.CHROME, ...options }, async context => {
    const page = await context.newPage();
    await page.goto(`${web.url}/?api=${encodeURIComponent(dev.url)}&witness=web`, { waitUntil: "domcontentloaded" });
    if (identity.guests) {
      await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Continue as a guest", exact: true }).click();
    } else if (identity.password) {
      await fillRN(page.getByLabel("Email", { exact: true }), `proof-${randomUUID()}@example.test`);
      await fillRN(page.getByLabel("Password", { exact: true }), "Proof-password-928!");

    } else {
      assert.ok(personas.length, "declare identity or personas before proving the starter");
      await page.getByRole("button", { name: personas[0], exact: true }).click();
    }
    // TEMPLATE_READY

      const svg = button.locator("svg");

      await waitForFresh(renderedText(page, new RegExp(title), { within }), null);
    }
  });
  console.log("frontend:proof passed");

/// Only the exact generated appendix is ignored for historical byte recognition.
pub(super) fn without_readme(text: &str) -> &str { text.strip_suffix(README_PROOFS).or_else(|| text.strip_suffix(PREVIOUS_30_README_PROOFS)).or_else(|| text.strip_suffix(PREVIOUS_README_PROOFS)).unwrap_or(text) }

pub(super) fn files(files: &mut Vec<(&'static str, String)>, options: &Options, backend: u16, frontend: u16, web: bool, shape: &super::starter::Shape) {
    let has_frontend = shape.body == super::starter::Body::Todos || options.flags.contains_key("template");
    for (_, text) in files.iter_mut().filter(|(name, _)| *name == "README.md") {
        if has_frontend { *text = readme(std::mem::take(text)); }
    }
    for (name, text) in files.iter_mut() {
        if *name == "vite.config.mts" { *text = runtime_vite(text, backend, frontend); }
    }
    let proof = frontend_proof(include_str!("frontend-proof.mjs"), options.flags.get("template").map(String::as_str), web);
    let dir = options.positionals.first().map(std::path::Path::new).unwrap_or_else(|| std::path::Path::new("."));
    let sources = if let Ok(Some(own)) = super::own_schema(dir) {
        own.files.iter().filter_map(|name| std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("snapback").join(name)).ok().map(|text| (name.clone(), text))).collect::<Vec<_>>()
    } else { files.iter().find(|(name, _)| *name == "snapback/schema.q").map(|(_, text)| vec![("schema.q".to_owned(), text.clone())]).unwrap_or_default() };
    let day2 = options.flags.contains_key("day2");
    for version in ["v1", "v2"].into_iter().filter(|_| day2) {
        if dir.join("versions").join(version).exists() { continue; }
        // Init is a one-shot CLI operation. Destinations live for this invocation's
        // plan, whose existing interface uses static generated names.
        for (name, text) in &sources {
            let path: &'static str = Box::leak(format!("versions/{version}/{name}").into_boxed_str());
            files.push((path, text.clone()));
        }
        let marker: &'static str = Box::leak(format!("versions/{version}/fixtures/.gitkeep").into_boxed_str());
        files.push((marker, String::new()));
        let mut fixtures = files.iter().filter_map(|(name, text)| name.strip_prefix("fixtures/").map(|name| (name.to_owned(), text.clone()))).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        if fixtures.is_empty() {
            if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(dir.join("fixtures")) {
                for entry in entries.flatten().filter(|entry| entry.path().extension().is_some_and(|ext| ext == "jsonl") || entry.file_name() == "test.sweep.json") {
                    if let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(entry.path()) { fixtures.push((entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned(), text)); }
                }
            }
        }
        for (name, text) in fixtures {
            let path: &'static str = Box::leak(format!("versions/{version}/fixtures/{name}").into_boxed_str());
            files.push((path, text));
        }
    }
    if has_frontend { files.push(("scripts/frontend-proof.mjs", proof)); }
    if day2 { files.push(("scripts/day2-proof.mjs", include_str!("day2-proof.mjs").to_owned())); }
    files.push(("scripts/launch.mjs", include_str!("launch.mjs").replace("BACKEND", &backend.to_string()).replace("FRONTEND", &frontend.to_string())));
    for (name, text) in files.iter_mut().filter(|(name, _)| *name == "package.json") {
        let mut package: Value = serde_json::from_str(text).unwrap();
        if has_frontend { package["scripts"]["frontend:proof"] = json!("node scripts/frontend-proof.mjs"); }
        if day2 { package["scripts"]["day2:proof"] = json!("node scripts/day2-proof.mjs versions/v1 versions/v2"); }
        if (package["snapback4"].is_null() || package["snapback4"].is_object()) && (package["snapback4"]["starter"].is_null() || package["snapback4"]["starter"].is_object()) {
            package["snapback4"]["starter"]["day2"] = json!(day2);
        }
        if has_frontend {
            package["scripts"]["proof:web"] = json!("node scripts/frontend-proof.mjs");
            package["devDependencies"]["playwright-core"] = json!("1.55.1");
        }
        package["scripts"]["backend"] = json!("node scripts/launch.mjs backend");
        if web {
            package["scripts"]["dev"] = json!("node scripts/launch.mjs vite");
            package["scripts"]["preview"] = json!("node scripts/launch.mjs vite-preview");
        } else {
            package["scripts"]["start"] = json!("node scripts/launch.mjs expo");
            package["scripts"]["web"] = json!("node scripts/launch.mjs expo-web");
            package["scripts"]["native:smoke"] = json!("node scripts/launch.mjs native-smoke");
        }
        *text = pretty(&package);
        let _ = name;
    }
}

pub(super) fn frontend_proof(source: &str, template: Option<&str>, web: bool) -> String {
    // Social keeps account controls on its Profile tab; prove the actual route.
    let mut proof = source.replace("// TEMPLATE_READY", if template == Some("social") {
        "await page.getByText(\"Profile\", { exact: true }).click();"
    } else { "" });
    if template == Some("social") {
        proof = proof.replace("getByLabel(\"Task\"", "getByLabel(\"Display name\"")
            .replace("name: \"Add\"", "name: \"Save profile\"")
            .replace("beginForm(\"add\", { title }", "beginForm(\"saveProfile\", { name: title }");
    } else if template == Some("chat") {
        proof = proof.replace("    const task =", r#"    const viewer = await page.evaluate(() => window.__snapback4Witness.viewer());
    const seeded = await fetch(`${dev.url}/seed`, { method: "POST", headers: { "content-type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify([
      { table: "conversations", row: { id: "proof-room", title: "Proof room", creatorId: viewer } },
      { table: "memberships", row: { id: "proof-member", conversationId: "proof-room", principal: viewer, role: "admin", joinedAt: Date.now() } }
    ]) });
    assert.ok(seeded.ok, await seeded.text());
    await page.getByText("Proof room", { exact: true }).click();
    const task ="#)
            .replace("page.getByLabel(\"Task\", { exact: true })", "page.getByPlaceholder(\"Message\", { exact: true })")
            .replace("name: \"Add\"", "name: \"Send\"")
            .replace("beginForm(\"add\", { title }", "beginForm(\"send\", { conversationId: \"proof-room\", body: title }");
        // Chat receipts echo drafts. Restrict evidence to its message display.
        if web { proof = proof.replace("renderedText(page, new RegExp(title))", "renderedText(page, new RegExp(title), { within: page.getByRole(\"region\", { name: \"Thread\" }) })"); }
    }
    let scope = match (template, web) {
        (Some("social"), _) => "page.getByTestId(\"profile-results\")",
        (Some("chat"), true) => "page.getByRole(\"region\", { name: \"Thread\" })",
        (Some("chat"), false) => "page.getByTestId(\"thread-results\")",
        (_, true) => "page.getByRole(\"list\")",
        (_, false) => "page.getByTestId(\"todo-results\")",
    };
    proof = proof.replace("RESULTS_SCOPE", scope);
    proof = proof.replace("BUILD_SCRIPT", if web { "build" } else { "build:web" });
    proof
}

fn previous_frontend(dir: &std::path::Path, web: bool) -> Option<Option<&'static str>> {
    super::proof_advice::frontend_template(dir, web).filter(|(version,_)| matches!(*version,"0.4.28"|"0.4.29"|"0.4.30"|"0.4.31"|"0.4.32")).map(|(_,template)|template)
}

/// Adapt adds missing proof infrastructure, preserving files and script names
/// already owned by the application. It never runs a package manager.
pub(super) fn plan(dir: &std::path::Path, own: &super::OwnSchema, enable_day2: bool) -> std::io::Result<Vec<(&'static str, String)>> {
    let web = dir.join("src/App.tsx").is_file();
    let router = dir.join("app/_layout.tsx").is_file();
    if !web && !dir.join("App.tsx").is_file() && !router { return Ok(Vec::new()); }
    let shape = super::starter::Shape { title: super::title(dir), password: own.identity.is_some_and(|(p, g)| p && !g),
        personas: own.identity.is_none().then(|| own.personas.clone()).filter(|p| !p.is_empty()),
        body: if super::adapt::fits_todos(own) { super::starter::Body::Todos } else { super::starter::Body::Home(None) }, offline: own.offline.clone() };
    let path = dir.join("package.json");
    let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)?;
    let mut package: Value = serde_json::from_str(&text).map_err(std::io::Error::other)?;
    let router = router && !web && package["main"] == "expo-router/entry";
    if !web && !dir.join("App.tsx").is_file() && !router { return Ok(Vec::new()); }
    let original = package.clone();
    let day2_text = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("scripts/day2-proof.mjs")).ok();
    let referenced_day2 = package["scripts"].as_object().is_some_and(|scripts| scripts.values().any(|v| v.as_str().is_some_and(|s| s.contains("scripts/day2-proof.mjs"))));
    let missing_managed_day2 = day2_text.is_none() && matches!(package["scripts"]["day2:proof"].as_str(),
        Some("node scripts/day2-proof.mjs" | "node scripts/day2-proof.mjs versions/v1.q versions/v2.q" | "node scripts/day2-proof.mjs versions/v1 versions/v2"));
    let managed_day2 = day2_text.as_deref().is_some_and(super::proof_advice::known_day2) || missing_managed_day2;
    let day2 = enable_day2 || referenced_day2 || package.pointer("/snapback4/starter/day2") != Some(&json!(false)) && managed_day2;
    // Deleting both the command and file records a durable opt-out on apply.
    // Preview/check never write the inferred choice. Explicit --day2 opts in again.
    if (package["snapback4"].is_null() || package["snapback4"].is_object()) && (package["snapback4"]["starter"].is_null() || package["snapback4"]["starter"].is_object()) {
        package["snapback4"]["starter"]["day2"] = json!(day2);
    }
    let backend = package["scripts"]["backend"].as_str().and_then(|s| s.strip_prefix("snapback4 dev --port ")).and_then(|s| s.parse::<u16>().ok())
.or_else(|| launcher_port(dir, "backend")).unwrap_or(4400);
    let frontend = launcher_port(dir, "frontend").or_else(|| package["scripts"][if web { "dev" } else { "start" }].as_str()
        .and_then(|s| s.split_once("--port ")).and_then(|(_, rest)| rest.split_whitespace().next()).and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok())
        .or_else(|| std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("vite.config.mts")).ok().and_then(|s| s.split_once("server: { port: ").and_then(|(_, rest)| rest.split(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_digit()).next()).and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok())))
        ).unwrap_or(if backend != 4400 { backend.saturating_add(1) } else if web { 5173 } else { 8081 });
    let mut generated = vec![("package.json", pretty(&package))];
    let mut flags = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
    if router { flags.insert("template".into(), "social".into()); }
    else if let Some(Some(template)) = previous_frontend(dir, web) { flags.insert("template".into(), template.into()); }
    if day2 { flags.insert("day2".into(), String::new()); }
    files(&mut generated, &Options { positionals: vec![dir.to_string_lossy().into_owned()], flags, json: false }, backend, frontend, web, &shape);
    // A saved version is immutable application evidence. Never fill its missing
    // fixture files from today's working release during an adaptation.
    generated.retain(|(name, _)| !name.starts_with("versions/") || {
        let version = name.split('/').nth(1).unwrap();
        !dir.join("versions").join(version).exists()
    });
    // New directories capture the current source and contemporary fixtures. Flat
    // legacy snapshots remain untouched evidence; they are never propagated.
    // Custom proofs own their saved source layout; do not manufacture snapshots.
    if !managed_day2 && !enable_day2 { generated.retain(|(name,_)| !name.starts_with("versions/")); }
    let wanted: Value = serde_json::from_str(&generated[0].1).unwrap();
    for group in ["scripts", "devDependencies"] {
        if !package[group].is_object() { package[group] = json!({}); }
        for (key, value) in wanted[group].as_object().unwrap() {
            let old = package[group].get(key).and_then(Value::as_str);
            let managed = group == "scripts" && old.is_some_and(|old| match key.as_str() {
                "day2:proof" => managed_day2 && matches!(old, "node scripts/day2-proof.mjs" | "node scripts/day2-proof.mjs versions/v1.q versions/v2.q"),
                "backend" => old.strip_prefix("snapback4 dev --port ").is_some_and(|n| n.parse::<u16>().is_ok()),
                "dev" | "preview" => old.strip_prefix(if key == "dev" { "vite --port " } else { "vite preview --port " }).and_then(|s| s.strip_suffix(" --strictPort")).is_some_and(|n| n.parse::<u16>().is_ok()),
                "start" | "web" => old.strip_prefix(if key == "start" { "expo start --port " } else { "expo start --web --port " }).is_some_and(|n| n.parse::<u16>().is_ok()),
                _ => false,
            });
            if managed || ((key == "day2:proof" && enable_day2 || key == "frontend:proof" && super::proof_advice::known_frontend(dir) || key == "playwright-core" && (super::proof_advice::known_frontend(dir) || super::proof_advice::referenced(dir, "scripts/frontend-proof.mjs"))) && old.is_none()) { package[group][key] = value.clone(); }
        }
    }
    let mut config_changes = Vec::new();
    if web {
        if let Ok(current) = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("vite.config.mts")) {
            // Replace only the exact initializer forms, allowing their port literals.
            let numbers = current.split("port: ").skip(1).filter_map(|s| s.split(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_digit()).next()?.parse::<u16>().ok()).collect::<Vec<_>>();
            let mut normalized = current.clone();
            for number in &numbers { normalized = normalized.replace(&format!("port: {number}"), "port: 5173"); }
            let reference = include_str!("starter/web/vite.config.mts").replace("port: 4173", "port: 5173");
            if normalized == reference { config_changes.push(("vite.config.mts", runtime_vite(&current, backend, numbers.first().copied().unwrap_or(5173)))); }
        }
    }
    let inherited_frontend = previous_frontend(dir, web).filter(|template| super::adapt::fits_todos(own) || template.is_some());
    if !super::adapt::fits_todos(own) && super::proof_advice::frontend_template(dir, web).is_some_and(|(_, template)| template.is_none()) {
        if let Some(scripts) = package["scripts"].as_object_mut() {
            scripts.retain(|_, value| value.as_str() != Some("node scripts/frontend-proof.mjs"));
        }
    }
    if let Some(template) = inherited_frontend {
        if let Some((_, text)) = generated.iter_mut().find(|(name, _)| *name == "scripts/frontend-proof.mjs") {
            *text = frontend_proof(include_str!("frontend-proof.mjs"), template, web);
        }
    }
    let referenced_after = |path: &str| package["scripts"].as_object().is_some_and(|scripts| scripts.values().any(|v|v.as_str().is_some_and(|s|s.contains(path))));
    let mut additions: Vec<_> = generated.into_iter().skip(1)
        .filter(|(name, _)| {
            if *name == "scripts/frontend-proof.mjs" { return inherited_frontend.is_some() || !dir.join(name).exists() && referenced_after(name); }
            if *name == "scripts/day2-proof.mjs" { return day2 && (managed_day2 || !dir.join(name).exists() && (enable_day2 || referenced_day2)); }
            if !dir.join(name).exists() {
                return name.starts_with("versions/") || referenced_after(name);
            }
            false
        }).collect();
    additions.extend(config_changes);
    if package != original { additions.push(("package.json", pretty(&package))); }
    Ok(additions)
}

fn launcher_port(dir: &std::path::Path, name: &str) -> Option<u16> {
    let text = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("scripts/launch.mjs")).ok()?;
    // Recognize the generated fallback expression, not client application code.
    let marker = if name == "backend" { "low === null ? " } else { ": low === null ? " };
    text.split_once(marker)?.1.split_whitespace().next()?.parse().ok()
}


pub(super) fn apply(dir: &std::path::Path, additions: &[(&str, String)]) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    for (name, body) in additions {
        let path = dir.join(name);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap())?;
        if *name == "package.json" || *name == "vite.config.mts" || *name == "scripts/frontend-proof.mjs" || *name == "scripts/day2-proof.mjs" { super::replace_file(&path, body)?; }
        else {
            use std::io::Write;
            let mut file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new().write(true).create_new(true).open(&path)?;
            file.write_all(body.as_bytes())?;
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Environment is evaluated whenever Vite loads the config, never at init time.
pub(super) fn runtime_vite(text: &str, backend: u16, frontend: u16) -> String {
    if text.contains("const proofRange") { return text.to_owned(); }
    let header = format!(r#"const proofRange = [process.env.PORT_LO, process.env.PORT_HI];
if (proofRange.some(v => v !== undefined) && (!proofRange.every(v => v && /^\d+$/.test(v)) || Number(proofRange[0]) < 1 || Number(proofRange[1]) > 65535 || Number(proofRange[0]) >= Number(proofRange[1]))) throw Error("PORT_LO/PORT_HI must provide at least two valid ports");
const backendPort = proofRange[0] === undefined ? {backend} : Number(proofRange[0]);
const frontendPort = proofRange[0] === undefined ? {frontend} : backendPort + 1;
process.env.VITE_SNAPBACK_URL ??= `http://127.0.0.1:${{backendPort}}`;
"#);
    let mut result = text.to_owned();
    // All generated configurations have literal ports; preserve unrelated config.
    for port in [frontend, 5173, 4173] { result = result.replace(&format!("port: {port}"), "port: frontendPort"); }
    format!("{header}{result}")
}

//! Advice is evidence about known template bytes, or explicitly a heuristic.
// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000.000#11-wave-14-truthful-starter-custody-day4 — custom proofs own their arguments and assertions.
use std::path::Path;
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
use serde::Deserialize;

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Template { file: String, version: String, template: Option<String>, web: bool, sha256: String }
fn templates() -> &'static [Template] {
    static TEMPLATES: std::sync::OnceLock<Vec<Template>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
    TEMPLATES.get_or_init(|| serde_json::from_str(include_str!("proof-digests.json")).expect("shipped proof digests"))
}
pub(super) fn digest(text: &str) -> String { format!("{:x}", Sha256::digest(text.as_bytes())) }
pub(super) fn known_day2(text: &str) -> bool {
    let hash = digest(text);
    templates().iter().any(|t| t.file == "day2" && t.sha256 == hash)
}
/// Exact shipped helper bytes identify its identity mode and starter revision.
pub(super) fn native_template(text: &str) -> Option<(&'static str, bool)> {
    let hash = digest(text);
    templates().iter().find(|t| t.file == "native" && t.sha256 == hash)
        .map(|t| (t.version.as_str(), t.template.as_deref() == Some("password")))
}
pub(super) fn frontend_template(dir: &Path, web: bool) -> Option<(&'static str, Option<&'static str>)> {
    let text = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("scripts/frontend-proof.mjs")).ok()?;
    let hash = digest(&text);
    templates().iter().find(|t| t.file == "frontend" && t.web == web && t.sha256 == hash)
        .map(|t| (t.version.as_str(), t.template.as_deref()))
}
pub(super) fn known_frontend(dir: &Path) -> bool { [false,true].into_iter().any(|web|frontend_template(dir,web).is_some()) }
fn package(dir: &Path) -> serde_json::Value {
    std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("package.json")).ok().and_then(|s|serde_json::from_str(&s).ok()).unwrap_or_default()
}
pub(super) fn referenced(dir: &Path, path: &str) -> bool {
    package(dir)["scripts"].as_object().is_some_and(|scripts| scripts.values().any(|v|v.as_str().is_some_and(|s|s.contains(path))))
}
// @ref LLP 3000.011.003.000#15-wave-15-starter-advice-day5-2026-10-18 — compare the complete directory capture; no distinguished schema.q is required.
pub(super) fn legacy_differences(dir: &Path, plan: &[(&str, String)]) -> Vec<String> {
    ["v1", "v2"].into_iter().filter_map(|version| {
        let flat = format!("versions/{version}.q");
        let prefix = format!("versions/{version}/");
        let legacy = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join(&flat)).ok()?;
        let mut saved = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
        if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(dir.join(&prefix)) {
            for entry in entries.flatten() {
                let path = entry.path();
                if path.extension().is_some_and(|ext|ext=="q") && let Ok(text)=std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {
                    saved.insert(format!("{prefix}{}",entry.file_name().to_string_lossy()),text);
                }
            }
        }
        for (name,text) in plan.iter().filter(|(name,_)|name.starts_with(&prefix) && name.ends_with(".q")) {
            saved.insert((*name).to_owned(),text.clone());
        }
        if saved.is_empty() || saved.len()==1 && saved.values().next()==Some(&legacy) {return None;}
        let paths=saved.keys().cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
        Some(format!("info: {flat} differs from {paths}; saved {version} captures snapback/*.q, not the legacy flat source; both remain unchanged evidence. Review the pair before day2:proof"))
    }).collect()
}
pub(super) fn report(dir: &Path) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut advice = legacy_differences(dir, &[]);
    if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(dir.join("versions")) {
        let mut paths = Vec::new();
        for entry in entries.flatten() {
            let path = entry.path();
            if path.is_dir() {
                if let Ok(files) = std::fs::read_dir(&path) { paths.extend(files.flatten().map(|entry|entry.path()).filter(|path|path.extension().is_some_and(|e|e=="q"))); }
            } else if path.extension().is_some_and(|e|e=="q") { paths.push(path); }
        }
        paths.sort();
        for path in paths {
            if let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {
                let hash = digest(&text);
                if let Some(t) = templates().iter().find(|t| t.file == "todo-schema" && t.sha256 == hash) {
                    advice.push(format!("info: {} is the unmodified {} todo snapshot (sha256 {hash}); replace it with this app's saved schema and contemporary fixtures before day2:proof", path.strip_prefix(dir).unwrap_or(&path).display(), t.version));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    for path in ["scripts/frontend-proof.mjs", "scripts/day2-proof.mjs", "scripts/launch.mjs"] {
        if !dir.join(path).exists() && referenced(dir, path) {
            advice.push(format!("info: {path} is missing but package.json still references it; preview `snapback4 init --adapt`, then `snapback4 init --adapt --apply`"));
        }
    }
    if let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("scripts/day2-proof.mjs")) {
        let hash=digest(&text);
        if let Some(t)=templates().iter().find(|t| t.file=="day2" && t.sha256==hash) {
            if matches!(t.version.as_str(),"0.4.28"|"0.4.29") {
                advice.push(format!("info: scripts/day2-proof.mjs is the unmodified {} starter: it asserts no business rows; preview `snapback4 init --adapt` to replace it and capture current sources/fixtures",t.version));
            }
            if text.contains("assert.fail(") {
                advice.push(format!("info: scripts/day2-proof.mjs is the unmodified {} assert.fail business-assertion placeholder (sha256 {hash}); replace BUSINESS_ASSERTION_BEGIN with this app's persisted-row and refusal assertions", t.version));
            }
            if t.version=="0.4.30" || t.version=="0.4.31" {
                let script=package(dir)["scripts"]["day2:proof"].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_owned();
                if script=="node scripts/day2-proof.mjs" {
                    advice.push("info: the unmodified day-two starter needs its two saved-source arguments; preview `snapback4 init --adapt`".into());
                }
            }
        }
    }
    if let Ok(text)=std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("scripts/frontend-proof.mjs")) {
        // Custom JavaScript can hide builds in arbitrary imports/functions. These
        // checks deliberately make no claim about its behavior or ownership.
        let active=text.lines().filter(|line| !line.trim_start().starts_with("//")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n");
        let flat=active.replace(['\"','\'',',','[',']','(',')'], " ");
        let words=flat.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let serves_dist=words.windows(2).any(|w|w==["startStatic","dist"]);
        let pkg=package(dir);
        let launch=pkg["scripts"]["frontend:proof"].as_str().unwrap_or("");
        let pre=pkg["scripts"]["prefrontend:proof"].as_str().unwrap_or("");
        let builds=|s:&str|s.contains("build")||s.contains("export");
        if serves_dist && !builds(&active) && !builds(launch) && !builds(pre) {
            advice.push("info: scripts/frontend-proof.mjs serves dist with no visible build step (heuristic; imported code may build it); build in the proof or its npm script before startStatic(\"dist\")".into());
        }
        if words.windows(3).any(|w|w==["npx","snapback4","dev"]) {
            advice.push("info: scripts/frontend-proof.mjs launches npx snapback4 dev (heuristic); use startDev from snapback4/proof for an owned server and bounded cleanup".into());
        }
    }
    for path in ["scripts/frontend-proof.mjs", "scripts/day2-proof.mjs", "scripts/proof.mjs", "scripts/acceptance.mjs"] {
        let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join(path)) else { continue; };
        let active = text.lines().filter(|line| !line.trim_start().starts_with("//")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n");
        let npx = active.contains("\"npx\"") || active.contains("'npx'");
        let status_only = active.contains("/auth/config") && (active.contains("status === 200") || active.contains("status == 200") || active.contains("[200, 404]") || active.contains("status === 404"));
        if npx && status_only {
            advice.push(format!("info: {path} spawns npx and accepts readiness HTTP status (heuristic; sha256 {}); readiness is not business evidence. Use snapback4/proof hosts and assert persisted rows plus refusals at each release", digest(&text)));
        }
    }
    advice
}

mod tests {
    use super::*;
    #[test]
    fn every_shipped_proof_template_has_a_digest() {
        let mut expected=Vec::new();
        for (version,frontend,day2) in [
            ("0.4.28",include_str!("previous/frontend-proof-0.4.28.mjs"),include_str!("previous/day2-proof-0.4.28.mjs")),
            ("0.4.29",include_str!("previous/frontend-proof-0.4.29.mjs"),include_str!("previous/day2-proof-0.4.29.mjs")),
            ("0.4.30",include_str!("previous/frontend-proof-0.4.30.mjs"),include_str!("previous/day2-proof-0.4.30.mjs")),
            ("0.4.31",include_str!("previous/frontend-proof-0.4.31.mjs"),include_str!("day2-proof.mjs")),
            ("0.4.32",include_str!("previous/frontend-proof-0.4.32.mjs"),include_str!("previous/day2-proof-0.4.32.mjs")),
            ("0.4.33",include_str!("frontend-proof.mjs"),include_str!("day2-proof.mjs")),
        ] {
            for web in [false,true] { for template in [None,Some("chat"),Some("social")] {
                expected.push(serde_json::json!({"file":"frontend","version":version,"web":web,"template":template,"sha256":digest(&super::super::proof::frontend_proof(frontend,template,web))}));
            }}
            expected.push(serde_json::json!({"file":"day2","version":version,"web":false,"template":null,"sha256":digest(day2)}));
        }
        for (version, source) in [
            ("0.4.9", include_str!("starter/previous/native-smoke-0.4.9.ts")),
            ("0.4.16", include_str!("starter/previous/native-smoke-0.4.16.ts")),
            ("0.4.28", include_str!("starter/previous/wave14/native-smoke.ts")),
            ("0.4.31", include_str!("native-smoke.ts")),
        ] {
            for password in [false, true].into_iter().filter(|password| !*password || version != "0.4.9") {
                let text = super::super::starter::native_smoke_version(password, source);
                let version = if version == "0.4.16" && password { "0.4.25" } else { version };
                expected.push(serde_json::json!({"file":"native","version":version,"web":false,"template":if password { Some("password") } else { None },"sha256":digest(&text)}));
            }
        }
        expected.push(serde_json::json!({"file":"todo-schema","version":"0.4.30","web":false,"template":null,"sha256":digest(&super::super::without_design_references(include_str!("starter/previous/schema-0.4.30.q")))}));
        expected.push(serde_json::json!({"file":"todo-schema","version":"0.4.33","web":false,"template":null,"sha256":digest(&super::super::without_design_references(include_str!("starter/previous/schema-0.4.33.q")))}));
        expected.push(serde_json::json!({"file":"todo-schema","version":"0.4.35","web":false,"template":null,"sha256":digest(&super::super::without_design_references(include_str!("starter/schema.q")))}));
        if std::env::var_os("SNAPBACK4_UPDATE_PROOF_DIGESTS").is_some() {
            std::fs::write(concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),"/src/verbs/init/proof-digests.json"),serde_json::to_string_pretty(&expected).unwrap()+"\n").unwrap();
        } else {
            assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(include_str!("proof-digests.json")).unwrap(),serde_json::json!(expected),"retain historical digests and register each new shipped template");
        }
    }
}
