# Rules

**Snapback 2 optimizes the edit-to-verified loop — the agent's building an app on it, and ours building it.**

Speed is the constraint. Everything below exists to keep the edit-to-verified loop short
and to stop this repository accreting apparatus faster than anyone can remove it. These
rules bind `snapback2/` and the LLPs numbered 1000 and up; Snapback 1 is baselined, not
exempt, and its numbers may only fall.

Each rule is **[check]** (enforced by `caps`) or **[review]** (enforced by a human).

## Budgets — every budget is a trade, not a limit

- **5 blocking checks, 60s total.** A sixth requires deleting one, in the same PR. **[check]**
- **59 documents in the working set** (`llp/current/`). Today's count. A 60th requires
  archiving one — which is just removing the link. Snapback 2 aims to leave this at 15;
  Snapback 1's links are archived at promotion. **[check]**
- **12 documents in the foundation** (`llp/foundation/`). **[check]**
- **This file: 700 words.** If it grows, something becomes a check or stops being a rule. **[check]**
- **1,500 lines per source file, baseline 204.** Generated files exempt — and generated
  files are built, not committed; so are benchmark run records under `benchmarks/runs/`,
  which are evidence, not source. The baseline is Snapback 1's oversize count on the day
  the rule landed; it may not grow, and `snapback2/` contributes zero to it. **[check]**

## Blocking checks

`caps` · `ref-check` · `snapback2/scripts/test.sh` · `snapback2/scripts/measure.mjs --check` · `check-inventories`

## Loop shape

- **Every check reports all failures in one run.** Fail-fast is banned. **[check]**
- **Nothing blocks on anything slower than 60 seconds.** Slow verification runs on a
  schedule, attributed to the breaking commit, and files a bounded set of issues. **[review]**
- **Fix loops get 3 rounds.** Then stop: escalate to a human or descope. **[review]**

## Time budgets

Tracked every run of `snapback2/scripts/measure.mjs` (appends `snapback2/metrics/loop.jsonl`).
A regression is a P0 with a name on it.

| | budget |
|---|---|
| Incremental rebuild after a one-line edit | 15s |
| Test what you just changed | 30s |
| Blocking gate suite | 60s |
| Full build, warm cache | 5 min |
| **`snapback2 check` on a program (the agent's product latency)** | **1s** |
| **`snapback2 doctor` boot-to-ready** | **0.5s** |

## Scope

- **`NOT-DOING.md` is binding.** Moving something onto the doing-list means writing why
  and taking something off. **[review]**
- **Delete; don't deprecate.** No compat shims or migration paths before promotion. **[review]**
- **Nothing is compiled, transpiled, or generated at runtime that could be built ahead of
  time.** **[review]**
- **A spec needs an implementer and a date, or it isn't written.** **[review]**
- **Only implemented specs bind.** A document with no running code behind it is a
  proposal, and a proposal cannot block a PR or justify a check. **[review]**

## Agents

- **Agents remove apparatus freely and add none.** An agent PR that adds a check, script,
  registry, config file, or design doc needs explicit human approval saying so. **[review]**
- **2026-09-06 session exception:** the user delegated the search implementation
  decisions; one `snapback2-core/build.rs` may generate pinned Unicode tables at
  build time, alongside the existing package build. No new gate, registry,
  runtime generator, or Unicode dependency is authorized by this exception. **[review]**
- **Snapback 2 LLPs are numbered 1000 and up**; `llp-create` must be told. **[review]**
- **Snapback 4 LLPs are numbered 3000 and up** (`snapback4/`, LLP 3000); it adopts these budgets
  and loop shape as its own and keeps its scope in `snapback4/NOT-DOING.md`. **[review]**

## Shared machines

- Warm, named lanes, one per stream of work. Never clone fresh; reuse the worktree.
- **Never `git stash`.** Use a temporary commit.
- Kill only PIDs you recorded at launch. Never by name or pattern.
# LLP 2000.000: Snapback 3 — keep the core, flip two substrates, start at hub scale

**Type:** RFC
**Status:** Draft
**Role:** Second opinion on LLP 2000; since 2026-09-12 also the design brief Snapback 4 builds (LLP 3000)
**Systems:** Snapback 3 product architecture, bounded computation, client data model, client API vocabulary, language and tooling, effects runtime, verification (simulation), performance budgets, process
**Author:** Claude Fable 5.1, at Charlie Cheever's request
**Date:** 2026-09-12
**Revised:** 2026-09-12 (adopted as the Snapback 4 design brief by LLP 3000 decision 3); 2026-09-12 (initial)
**Related:** [LLP 2000](./2000-snapback3.rfc.md) (parent), [LLP 3000](./3000-snapback4.explainer.md) (the Snapback 4 root that builds this brief), LLP 0000, [LLP 0329](./0329-agent-native-rebuild-diagnosis.research.md), [LLP 0329.014.004](./0329.014.004-bounded-data-programs-v1-design.rfc.md), [LLP 0329.016](./0329.016-agentic-dev-loop-from-scratch.rfc.md), [LLP 1000](./1000-snapback2.explainer.md), [LLP 1001](./1001-query-engine.spec.md), [LLP 1002](./1002-dev-loop.spec.md), [LLP 1012](./1012-local-first-v1.spec.md), [LLP 1018.003](./1018.003-truthful-and-composed-client.decision.md), [LLP 1018.008](./1018.008-elegance-after-the-corrections.research.md), [LLP 1018.008.007](./1018.008.007-affordable-offline-acquisition.research.md), [LLP 1018.008.008](./1018.008.008-locality-of-application-changes.research.md), [LLP 1018.008.009](./1018.008.009-residual-ergonomic-gaps.research.md), [LLP 1019](./1019-derived-delivery-custody.rfc.md), [LLP 1020](./1020-day-two-evolution-and-legible-ceilings.rfc.md), [LLP 1023](./1023-clique-builder-jump.rfc.md), [LLP 1024](./1024-single-lane-delivered-search.rfc.md), [LLP 1025](./1025-digest-final-emission-at-hub-scale.research.md), `rules/RULES.md`, `rules/NOT-DOING.md`, `benchmarks/runs/2026-09-05-clique-full-3x3/holistic-scores.md`

## 1. Summary

LLP 2000 is right that the whole application is the unit of design, right
that ownership comes before abstraction, and right to ask for deterministic
simulation and an early real deployment. Its weakness is that it treats the
two structural choices that produced Snapback 2's costs as open research
questions, and then proposes a first experiment at exactly the scale where
those costs are invisible. This document takes a position on both, names
what to keep from Snapback 2 verbatim, and rewrites the first slice so it
can fail for the right reasons.

The position, in one paragraph. Snapback 2's *core* is excellent and should
be copied: the rule language and its uniformity analysis, the structural-fact
family, one data language, typed states with no silence, refusals that paste
a rewrite, personas, the successor classifier, the derived per-recipient
log, the loop verbs and their sub-second budgets. Two *substrates* under
that core are where the record shows the hours went, and both should be
flipped rather than re-investigated: (1) the static certificate should keep
certifying **authorization and shape** and stop pricing **bytes and steps**,
which move to a deterministic runtime meter with honest `capped`/abort
outcomes; and (2) the client should hold **a replica of the viewer's declared
partition** — the local-first shape every shipped sync engine and Snapback
2's own `deliver` log converge on — instead of a per-query result cache
proven by receipts. Those two flips dissolve most of the machinery that
leaked into the application (receipts, coverage, halos, validators, grants,
ID slices, drains, `withHistory`, follower inboxes, per-table retention
words) and turn the 28-second acquisition into a bulk stream whose floor is
the device's write speed. The first slice should be built on the **hub
fixture** (1,000 memberships, 500 follows, 100,000 messages), with the
day-two change designed before the day-one screen, a native client in the
first slice, and a deterministic simulator as the primary test harness.

Three claims this document makes that LLP 2000 does not:

1. **The costs have two named causes, and both are decisions, not
   mysteries.** Byte-priced static certification and the receipt-proven
   result cache account for every ergonomic residual in LLP 1018.008.009
   except documentation. §2 shows the mapping.
2. **The first experiment must include the hub.** Snapback 2 was "elegant on
   day one and hostile on day two" (LLP 1020) and broke at 1,000 memberships
   (LLPs 1023, 1024, 1025). A two-principal slice will pass and teach nothing.
3. **The process is part of the product.** Seventy-one LLPs, over two
   thousand commits, and seven ceiling raises in fourteen days produced a
   sound system nobody can hold in their head. Snapback 3 needs one owner on
   the core, a simulator instead of a test matrix, and budgets anchored to
   competitors so that raising one means admitting a loss.

## 2. What the record says, read as causes

The evidence LLP 2000 §2 cites is right; its reading is too gentle. Every
row below is a Snapback 2 cost recorded in the corpus, with the substrate
that produced it. Numbers are the corpus's own and retain its scope limits.

| Recorded cost | Where | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Adding `editedAt: time ?` (44 bytes × 244 retained copies = 10,736) pushed `messages.searchAll` to 4,199,688 closure bytes against 4,194,304; the builder shrank a page from 20 to 19 | LLP 1018.008.008; 0.0.21 day-two diary | **Static byte pricing.** Closure bytes are a bound on what a receipt could ship; the product paid for the bound, not the work |
| The 1,000-membership digest fold certifies at 9,922,698 heap and 8,691,704 closure bytes and is refused; the recipient-keyed form is admitted at 2,733,253 / 1,848,418 | LLP 1025 §3 | **Static byte pricing** (heap = steps × 32 + closure scratch). A runtime meter would have run the fold and reported actual bytes |
| A message page is 50, not 200, because a row "prices at 16,016 bytes" and 200 exceed the 1 MiB output ceiling | LLP 1012 §3 | **Static byte pricing** of the worst-case row width |
| A per-recipient search projection is refused at 20,863,641 reserved steps against 1,000,000 | LLP 1024 §1 | **Static step pricing** of a derivation the engine would perform incrementally |
| Full acquisition of 10,008 messages: 67.4 s → 53.6 s → 32.6 s → 28.4 s against a 2–3 s objective; 201 requests, 200 acknowledgement mutations, 612 IndexedDB transactions; PowerSync reports 10,000 rows in 0.36 s native and 2.5 s on web | LLP 1018.008.007; LLP 1018.008.009 §4 | **Result cache, not replica.** Every 50-row page is a certified query, a receipt, a durable acknowledgement mutation, and a store swap |
| Adding a count to a thread makes the composite `partial` offline whenever count authority is missing, so the template declares an independent `history` query and `withHistory` bindings; 27 files / 1,718 lines → 28 / 1,751 after the fix | LLP 1018.008 F2; LLP 1018.008.009 §2 | **Result cache.** The count is not a fact the receipt covers, so the client cannot compose locally |
| `shared/thread.ts` describes table identity, row selection, order, create membership, draft fields and mutation targets a second time | LLP 1018.008 F2 | **Result cache.** Items must be reconstructed from answers because there is no local table to read |
| Sending stalled with 85 IDs remaining against a certified 352-ID slice on an 8,192-ID grant; recovery needed a "Sync now" action | LLP 1018.008 F1 | **Result cache + engine-minted IDs.** Prediction needs server ids before commit, so ids are granted in slices |
| A follower browser tab writes through a durable inbox row; the SDK carries `forwarding`, `writer-unresponsive`, `inbox-full`, `follower` states | LLP 1018.004 | **Result cache.** One writer per partition image; other tabs cannot mutate a receipt-proven image |
| Global search over 1,000 memberships costs ~1,010 HTTP requests through a client N-way merge | LLP 1024 §2 | **Result cache** (no local index over the partition) + **static pricing** (the server-side projection is refused) |
| The complete local runtime grew 7.8 KB → 89,843 gzip bytes; the ceiling was raised 34,000 → 50,000 → 66,000 → 82,000 → 82,500 → 84,000 → 85,000 → 90,000 | LLP 1000 §"Revised"; `rules/NOT-DOING.md` §Moves; LLP 1018.008 §10 | **Result cache.** The inputs list of `metrics/twin.jsonl` is coverage spans, extent facts, held directories, posting trees, fact integrity, swap journals — receipt machinery, not the interpreter |
| `Snapshot` carries `data, next, partial, receipt{state, source, seq, next, reason, rule, sites}, freshness{live, staleSince, connection}, local{predicted, retained, caughtUp, watermark}, refusal, status, reason` | LLP 1018.003 §1 | Both. Every field is a true fact about the mechanism; almost none is a fact about the application |
| `Schema::rule_hash` binds every queued write to the complete schema; an optional column on the subject table invalidates unrelated evidence | LLP 1018.002; LLP 1018.008.008 | **Result cache.** Evidence identity exists because held answers must be re-authorized; a replica re-runs the mutation at the server and needs no evidence identity |

Against that, what scored: on the 2026-09-05 three-scorer Clique run
Snapback 2 beat Convex on authorization (82 vs 79) and offline (81 vs 44)
and lost on queries and live (60 vs 85), client integration (59 vs 79),
setup and docs (55 vs 79), diagnostics and loop (66 vs 77), operations (53
vs 76) and scale (62 vs 80); overall 66 vs 81. The later single-lane 0.0.21
and 0.0.25 scores of 82 and 85 are real improvement and not a three-scorer
comparison. The wins are the core; the losses are composition, discovery,
scale and operations — the substrates and what sits on them.

LLP 2000 §2 summarises this as "costs arise where one layer must reconstruct
another layer's facts." True, and the layer doing the reconstructing is the
client, because it was designed as a cache that may not compute. Name the
cause and the remedy follows.

## 3. Where LLP 2000 is right, and should not be diluted

- **The whole application is the unit.** §3's four properties (composition,
  locality, continuity, performance) are the right acceptance vocabulary.
  Keep them as the headings of the scenario suite.
- **Ownership before abstraction.** §5's table is the best paragraph in the
  document. §8 below turns its fourth row into a fixed vocabulary.
- **Composed reads must not fabricate.** Unknown totals stay unknown; revoked
  rows do not linger. Both flips below preserve this; they change what is
  *known*, not what is *claimed*.
- **Writes have one lifecycle with durable admission distinct from commit
  and stable operation identity.** Keep LLP 1018.004's three outcomes.
- **Rust and SQLite.** Yes, and the engine's transaction, interpreter, rule
  evaluation and successor logic are the pieces to copy first (§5).
- **Prototype the experience before the core.** Yes — and §8 makes the
  prototype's API signatures binding on the implementation, not the reverse.
- **Deterministic simulation early**, citing TigerBeetle. This is the single
  most important sentence in LLP 2000 and §11 makes it the primary harness.
- **A real deployment and a native client early.** Yes; §11 puts the native
  client in slice one.
- **Parallel, fenced, 2000-series, promotion is the author's later call.** Yes.

## 4. Where LLP 2000 is wrong or leaves the wrong things open

### 4.1 It reopens the language and leaves the bound model open; invert that

## Summary

Snapback is a complete backend for application projects. It is designed to
**scale to zero** — to be so light that an idle app costs almost nothing and
needs no babysitting, letting you prototype without worry — while being built so
the same system can **scale up** to the workload of any realistically popular
production app.

It is **comprehensive and coherent**: it aims to give you everything a backend
needs under one roof, with the pieces designed to work together rather than
bolted on, a bit like Ruby on Rails. And it is **truly open** — MIT licensed,
with no source-available restrictions that would stop you from hosting it for
other people.

This document is the root of the Snapback LLP corpus. It captures the project's
intent, its subsystem boundaries, and the non-obvious constraints that every
follow-on design and every line of code is expected to respect. It reflects the
founder's stated direction for the project as of the date above. Treat the
direction here as active; treat subsystem details as boundary-level guidance
until follow-on LLPs turn them into implementation specs.

The corpus is flat under `llp/`. `llp/foundation/` links the kernel documents
from which the design could be recreated; `llp/current/` links the declared
working set. A document keeps its path for its whole life — `Tombstoned` and
`Superseded` are header statuses, not directories. `reviews/`, `current/`, and
`foundation/` are reserved names. Orient from `foundation/`, then `current/`,
then the `@ref`s in scope.

import { pendingRead, readyRead } from "./read-existence.ts";
import type { Client, Query, Read, Observed, ObserveOptions, Cursor } from "./contract.ts";
import { isReady } from "./contract.ts";
import { peekObservation } from "./observe-watch.ts";
const LOADING: Read<never> = { loading: true };

/** The requested page chain, with one newest observed image per row ID. */
export class Pages<A extends { c?: Cursor | null }, R extends readonly unknown[]> {
  private pages: { cursor: Cursor | null; observed: Observed<R>; unsubscribe: () => void }[] = [];
  private requested = 1;
  private subs = new Set<() => void>();
  private cache: { items: R[number][]; hasMore: boolean; read: Read<R> } | null = null;
  private peeked: Read<R> | undefined;
  private cacheReads: Read<R>[] = [];
  private reconciling = false;
  private imageRevision = 0;
  private imageRevisions = new WeakMap<object, number>();
  private noteImage(read: Read<R>) {
    // Revalidation/freshness changes retain the same data array; they do not
    // make an older row image newer than an image delivered on another page.
    if (isReady(read) && Array.isArray(read.data) && !this.imageRevisions.has(read.data))
      this.imageRevisions.set(read.data, ++this.imageRevision);
    return read;
  }
  constructor(private client: Client, private op: Query<A, R>, private args: A, private options?: ObserveOptions) {}
  private open(c: Cursor | null) {
    const observed = this.client.observe(this.op, { ...this.args, c }, this.options);
    const page = { cursor: c, observed, unsubscribe: () => {} };
    this.pages.push(page);
    page.unsubscribe = observed.subscribe(() => {
      if (this.pages.includes(page)) this.notify();
    });
  }
  private drop(from: number) {
    for (const page of this.pages.splice(from)) {
      page.unsubscribe();
      page.observed.close();
    }
  }
  private notify() {
    if (this.reconciling) return;
    this.reconciling = true;
    try {
      // A later page belongs to its predecessor's current cursor. Keep the
      // requested depth, but discard the old suffix before opening a new one:
      // deduplication alone cannot recover rows an old boundary skipped.
      for (let i = 0; i < this.pages.length; i++) {
        const read = this.noteImage(this.pages[i]!.observed.getSnapshot());
        const next = isReady(read) && Array.isArray(read.data) ? read.next : null;
        if (!next || i + 1 >= this.requested || this.pages.slice(0, i + 1).some((p) => p.cursor === next)) {
          this.drop(i + 1);
          break;
        }
        if (this.pages[i + 1]?.cursor !== next) {
          this.drop(i + 1);
          this.open(next);
        }
      }
      this.cache = null;
    } finally { this.reconciling = false; }
    for (const s of this.subs) s();
  }
  subscribe = (notify: () => void) => {
    this.subs.add(notify);
    if (!this.pages.length) { this.open(null); this.notify(); }
    let active = true;
    return () => {
      if (!active) return;
      active = false;
      this.subs.delete(notify);
      if (!this.subs.size) { this.drop(0); this.cache = null; }
    };
  };
  getSnapshot = () => {
    const peeked = this.pages.length ? undefined : peekObservation(this.client, this.op, { ...this.args, c: null }, this.options);
    // An unsubscribed render owns no notifications: recheck the live snapshot
    // and the linger cutoff on every call, caching only its derived page shape.
    if (peeked !== this.peeked) { this.peeked = peeked; this.cache = null; }
    // @ref LLP 3000.023#5 — page accessors check deadlines before a combined cache can escape.
    let sources, reads: Read<R>[];
    do {
      sources = [...this.pages];
      reads = sources.length ? sources.map(page => this.noteImage(page.observed.getSnapshot())) : peeked ? [this.noteImage(peeked)] : [];
      // A deadline check may synchronously drop a suffix through notify().
    } while (sources.length !== this.pages.length || sources.some((page, i) => page !== this.pages[i]));
    if (reads.length !== this.cacheReads.length || reads.some((read, i) => read !== this.cacheReads[i])) this.cache = null;
    this.cacheReads = reads;
    if (this.cache) return this.cache;
    const items: R[number][] = [];
    const identities = new Map<string, { index: number; revision: number }>();
    let last: Read<R> = LOADING as Read<R>;
    let complete = true, fresh = true, revalidating = false, pending = false;
    let cut: import("./contract.ts").ReadCut = null;
    let since: number | undefined;
    let knownSince = true;
    let loadingMore = false;
    for (const read of reads) {
      // @ref LLP 3000.019#3.3 — a pending next page keeps the ready prefix on screen.
      // Resets of the first page and refusals still replace the combined read.
      if ("loading" in read && isReady(last)) { loadingMore = true; break; }
      last = read;
      if (!isReady(read)) break;
      if (!Array.isArray(read.data)) { last = LOADING as Read<R>; break; }
      // @ref LLP 3000.028#3.3 — keyset edits may repeat IDs across pages.
      // Keep the first display position and the most recently observed image,
  const opts: ProofOptions = Array.isArray(options) ? { args: options } : options as ProofOptions;
  const args = [...(opts.args ?? [])];
  const persistent = args.some(arg => arg === "--store" || arg.startsWith("--store=") || arg === "--no-memory");
  if (persistent && args.includes("--memory")) throw new TypeError("proof startDev: --memory conflicts with --store/--no-memory");
  // Native persistence is the default. --no-memory remains a consumed explicit alias.
  const host = nativeHost("dev", [], { ...opts, args: args.filter(arg => arg !== "--no-memory") });
  return host.then(host => ({ ...host, personas: host.personas!, now: async () => {
    const { response, body } = await fetchIdentity(`${host.url}/dev/status`, deadline(opts.timeoutMs, 10_000));
    if (!response.ok || typeof body.now !== "number") throw Error("proof dev clock unavailable; password-only dev requires explicit --unsafe-dev-doors for clock/fixture tools; use serve staging for real users");
    return body.now;
  } }));
}
export interface ScheduleOutcome {
  name: string;
  target: string;
  period: string;
  fired: boolean;
  reason: string;
  holdCode?: "disabled" | "saved-boundary" | "initialized" | "not-due";
  savedBoundary?: number;
  nextBoundary: string;
  heldUntil?: string;
  periodStart?: number;
  periodEnd?: number;
  firedWindows: { periodStart: number; periodEnd: number }[];
  skippedPeriods?: number;
  skippedBoundaries: { periodStart: number; periodEnd: number; command: string }[];
  skippedBoundariesOmitted?: number;
  run?: { id: string; state: string; rowsWritten: number; error: string | null; errorTruncated: boolean };
}
export interface ClockAdvance { now: number; fired: ScheduleOutcome[]; held: ScheduleOutcome[] }
export interface ServeHost extends ProofHost {
  /** Authoritative staging time; requires a staging store and local operator authority. */
  now(): Promise<number>;
  /** Advance staging time once and drain due work. A lost reply must not be retried. */

  operatorToken(service?: string, days?: number): Promise<string>;
  seedAccounts(options: SeedAccountsOptions): Promise<StagingSessions>;
  sessions?: StagingSessions;
}

/** Starts a release. stop() awaits native exit and kernel store release.
 * @throws E_PROOF_USAGE for missing deployment directory; child exit, readiness deadline or served identity mismatch. stop() rejects bounded cleanup failure. */
export async function startServe(deployDir: string, options: ServeOptions | readonly string[] = {}): Promise<ServeHost> {
  if (typeof deployDir !== "string" || !deployDir.trim()) throw Object.assign(new TypeError("E_PROOF_USAGE: startServe(deployDir, options) requires a deployment directory as its first argument"), { code: "E_PROOF_USAGE" });
  const opts: ServeOptions = Array.isArray(options) ? { args: options } : options as ServeOptions;
  const directory = resolve(opts.cwd ?? ".", deployDir);
  if (opts.clockOffset !== undefined && (typeof opts.clockOffset !== "string" || !/^[+-]?\d+(ms|s|m|h|d|w)$/.test(opts.clockOffset))) throw new TypeError("E_PROOF_USAGE: clockOffset is a signed duration such as +25h");
  if (opts.clockOffset !== undefined && opts.args?.some(arg => arg === "--clock-offset" || arg.startsWith("--clock-offset="))) throw new TypeError("E_PROOF_USAGE: pass clockOffset once");
  const host = await nativeHost("serve", [directory], { ...opts, args: [...(opts.args ?? []), ...(opts.clockOffset === undefined ? [] : ["--clock-offset", opts.clockOffset])] });
  const clockCall = async (body?: object): Promise<ClockAdvance> => {
    const config = await fetchIdentity(`${host.url}/auth/config`, deadline(opts.timeoutMs, 10_000));
    if (!config.response.ok || config.body.environment !== "staging") throw Error("E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY: clock controls require a deploy --staging store");
    const clockToken = served.operatorToken("clock");
    const response = await fetch(`${host.url}/dev/clock/${body ? "advance" : "status"}`, { method: body ? "POST" : "GET", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${await clockToken}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, ...(body ? { body: JSON.stringify(body) } : {}), signal: AbortSignal.timeout(deadline(opts.timeoutMs, 60_000)) });
    const result = await response.json() as Partial<ClockAdvance> & { sessionNotice?: string; denied?: { code?: string; message?: string } };
    if (result.sessionNotice) process.stderr.write(`snapback4: ${result.sessionNotice}\n`);
    if (!response.ok || result.denied || !Number.isSafeInteger(result.now)) throw Error(`staging clock refused or reply unavailable; inspect clock and queued work before retrying: ${result.denied?.code ?? response.status} ${result.denied?.message ?? ""}`);
    if (body && (!Array.isArray(result.fired) || !Array.isArray(result.held))) throw Error("staging clock reply has no schedule report; inspect clock and queued work before retrying");
    for (const schedule of result.held ?? []) if (schedule.holdCode === "saved-boundary") process.stderr.write(`snapback4: schedule ${schedule.name}: ${schedule.reason}\n`);
    return { now: result.now!, fired: result.fired ?? [], held: result.held ?? [] };
  };
  // Exit can precede inherited watchdog flock release. The private local
  // barrier observes the same canonical ownership sidecar without writing data.
  let stopping: Promise<void> | undefined;
  const stop = () => stopping ??= (async () => {
    await host.stop();
    const result = await cli(["serve", directory, "--wait-stopped"], {...opts, timeoutMs:6000});
    if (result.code !== 0) throw Error(`proof serve store release failed: ${result.stderr}`);
  })().catch(error => { stopping = undefined; throw error; });
  const served: ServeHost = { ...host, stop,
    now: async () => (await clockCall()).now,
    advance: (duration, options = {}) => {
      if (typeof duration !== "string" || !/^\+?\d+(ms|s|m|h|d|w)$/.test(duration)) throw new TypeError("E_PROOF_USAGE: advance requires a positive whole duration");
      return clockCall({ duration, eachBoundary: options.eachBoundary ?? false });
    },
    operatorToken: async (service = "operator", days = 1) => {
      if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/.test(service) || !Number.isSafeInteger(days) || days < 1 || days > 3650) throw Error("proof operatorToken: invalid service or days (1..3650)");
      const result = await cli(["token", "--service", service, "--days", String(days), "--release", directory, "--quiet"], opts);
      if (result.code !== 0) throw Error(`proof operator token refused: ${result.stderr}`);
      const token = result.stdout.trim();
      if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/.test(token)) throw Error("proof operator token malformed");
      return token;
    },
    seedAccounts: accountOptions => seedAccounts(served, accountOptions),

pub(super) fn files(files: &mut Vec<(&'static str, String)>, options: &Options, backend: u16, frontend: u16, web: bool, shape: &super::starter::Shape) {
    let has_frontend = shape.body == super::starter::Body::Todos || options.flags.contains_key("template");
    for (_, text) in files.iter_mut().filter(|(name, _)| *name == "README.md") {
        if has_frontend { *text = readme(std::mem::take(text)); }
    }
    for (name, text) in files.iter_mut() {
        if *name == "vite.config.mts" { *text = runtime_vite(text, backend, frontend); }
    }
    let proof = frontend_proof(include_str!("frontend-proof.mjs"), options.flags.get("template").map(String::as_str), web);
    let dir = options.positionals.first().map(std::path::Path::new).unwrap_or_else(|| std::path::Path::new("."));
    let sources = if let Ok(Some(own)) = super::own_schema(dir) {
        own.files.iter().filter_map(|name| std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("snapback").join(name)).ok().map(|text| (name.clone(), text))).collect::<Vec<_>>()
    } else { files.iter().find(|(name, _)| *name == "snapback/schema.q").map(|(_, text)| vec![("schema.q".to_owned(), text.clone())]).unwrap_or_default() };
    let day2 = options.flags.contains_key("day2");
    for version in ["v1", "v2"].into_iter().filter(|_| day2) {
        if dir.join("versions").join(version).exists() { continue; }
        // Init is a one-shot CLI operation. Destinations live for this invocation's
        // plan, whose existing interface uses static generated names.
        for (name, text) in &sources {
            let path: &'static str = Box::leak(format!("versions/{version}/{name}").into_boxed_str());
            files.push((path, text.clone()));
        }
        let marker: &'static str = Box::leak(format!("versions/{version}/fixtures/.gitkeep").into_boxed_str());
        files.push((marker, String::new()));
        let mut fixtures = files.iter().filter_map(|(name, text)| name.strip_prefix("fixtures/").map(|name| (name.to_owned(), text.clone()))).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        if fixtures.is_empty() {
            if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(dir.join("fixtures")) {
                for entry in entries.flatten().filter(|entry| entry.path().extension().is_some_and(|ext| ext == "jsonl") || entry.file_name() == "test.sweep.json") {
                    if let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(entry.path()) { fixtures.push((entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned(), text)); }
                }
            }
        }
        for (name, text) in fixtures {
            let path: &'static str = Box::leak(format!("versions/{version}/fixtures/{name}").into_boxed_str());
            files.push((path, text));
        }
    }
    if has_frontend { files.push(("scripts/frontend-proof.mjs", proof)); }
    if day2 { files.push(("scripts/day2-proof.mjs", include_str!("day2-proof.mjs").to_owned())); }
    files.push(("scripts/launch.mjs", include_str!("launch.mjs").replace("BACKEND", &backend.to_string()).replace("FRONTEND", &frontend.to_string())));
    for (name, text) in files.iter_mut().filter(|(name, _)| *name == "package.json") {
        let mut package: Value = serde_json::from_str(text).unwrap();
        if has_frontend { package["scripts"]["frontend:proof"] = json!("node scripts/frontend-proof.mjs"); }
        if day2 { package["scripts"]["day2:proof"] = json!("node scripts/day2-proof.mjs versions/v1 versions/v2"); }
        if (package["snapback4"].is_null() || package["snapback4"].is_object()) && (package["snapback4"]["starter"].is_null() || package["snapback4"]["starter"].is_object()) {
            package["snapback4"]["starter"]["day2"] = json!(day2);
        }
        if has_frontend {
            package["scripts"]["proof:web"] = json!("node scripts/frontend-proof.mjs");
            package["devDependencies"]["playwright-core"] = json!("1.55.1");
        }
        package["scripts"]["backend"] = json!("node scripts/launch.mjs backend");
        if web {
            package["scripts"]["dev"] = json!("node scripts/launch.mjs vite");
            package["scripts"]["preview"] = json!("node scripts/launch.mjs vite-preview");
        } else {
            package["scripts"]["start"] = json!("node scripts/launch.mjs expo");
            package["scripts"]["web"] = json!("node scripts/launch.mjs expo-web");
            package["scripts"]["native:smoke"] = json!("node scripts/launch.mjs native-smoke");
        }
        *text = pretty(&package);
        let _ = name;
    }
}

        proof = proof.replace("    const task =", r#"    const viewer = await page.evaluate(() => window.__snapback4Witness.viewer());

            .replace("page.getByLabel(\"Task\", { exact: true })", "page.getByPlaceholder(\"Message\", { exact: true })")
            .replace("name: \"Add\"", "name: \"Send\"")

        // Chat receipts echo drafts. Restrict evidence to its message display.
        if web { proof = proof.replace("renderedText(page, new RegExp(title))", "renderedText(page, new RegExp(title), { within: page.getByRole(\"region\", { name: \"Thread\" }) })"); }

    let scope = match (template, web) {

        (Some("chat"), false) => "page.getByTestId(\"thread-results\")",
        (_, true) => "page.getByRole(\"list\")",
        (_, false) => "page.getByTestId(\"todo-results\")",

    let router = router && !web && package["main"] == "expo-router/entry";

    let day2_text = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("scripts/day2-proof.mjs")).ok();
    let referenced_day2 = package["scripts"].as_object().is_some_and(|scripts| scripts.values().any(|v| v.as_str().is_some_and(|s| s.contains("scripts/day2-proof.mjs"))));
    let missing_managed_day2 = day2_text.is_none() && matches!(package["scripts"]["day2:proof"].as_str(),

    let managed_day2 = day2_text.as_deref().is_some_and(super::proof_advice::known_day2) || missing_managed_day2;
    let day2 = enable_day2 || referenced_day2 || package.pointer("/snapback4/starter/day2") != Some(&json!(false)) && managed_day2;
    // Deleting both the command and file records a durable opt-out on apply.
    // Preview/check never write the inferred choice. Explicit --day2 opts in again.

        package["snapback4"]["starter"]["day2"] = json!(day2);
    }
    let backend = package["scripts"]["backend"].as_str().and_then(|s| s.strip_prefix("snapback4 dev --port ")).and_then(|s| s.parse::<u16>().ok())
.or_else(|| launcher_port(dir, "backend")).unwrap_or(4400);
    let frontend = launcher_port(dir, "frontend").or_else(|| package["scripts"][if web { "dev" } else { "start" }].as_str()
        .and_then(|s| s.split_once("--port ")).and_then(|(_, rest)| rest.split_whitespace().next()).and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok())
        .or_else(|| std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("vite.config.mts")).ok().and_then(|s| s.split_once("server: { port: ").and_then(|(_, rest)| rest.split(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_digit()).next()).and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok())))

        }

    if !super::adapt::fits_todos(own) && super::proof_advice::frontend_template(dir, web).is_some_and(|(_, template)| template.is_none()) {

# Rules

**Start here:** Reactions inherit their message's conversation membership; this excerpt uses the complete schema below. The dotted rule and audience are sugar for `read through` and inferred `sync`, including parent lifetime and insert authority.

```quarry
table reactions:
  message: messages
  immutable message
  read <- exists members[.message.conversation, viewer]
  sync to members[.message.conversation] last 500 by .id
```

- `E_READ_THROUGH`: the path must spell the whole parent rule; use a required immutable reference without a default, and immutable parent rule/expiry fields.
- `E_QUARRY_SELF_EQUALITY`: a nested predicate compares its row to itself; capture the outer value in a local before entering that predicate.
- `E_RULE`: a write lacks authority (mutations write as the caller; omitted rules deny); require a live readable parent and the child's insert rule, and under `dev` read the refusing clause with `snapback4 why recent`.

## Reference

### Point-read ladder

| Source form | Hidden, missing or expired row | Readable row |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `row = t[key]` | null; execution continues | row |
| `row = t[key] ! else CODE` | CODE; execution stops | row; execution continues |
| `exists t[key]` in a program | false | true when its extra equalities match |

Later requires cannot replace earlier refusals. Defaults can mask hidden reads.
N_LOOKUP_FILTERED names optional private side-table reads; prefer minimal
readable projections. N_LOOKUP_HIDDEN reviews required read/write gates.
Blind writes need no lookup. Rule `exists` uses separate witnesses.
See `guide refusals` and local `why recent`.

### Column read rules

A column may append `read <- policy`; `read (a, b) <- policy` on the table shares a gate. Both narrow row authority, omit denied row properties and make
explicit selections optional/null. The complete runnable example and sync, asset, aggregate and rollback boundaries are in `guide rule-recipes`,
Column-level privacy. Row-local cells sync; probe-based cells stay online and ordinary queries fall back automatically. Protected payloads cannot supply
stored keys, cursors/order/search, authority, lifetimes, immutable constraints or maintained derivation inputs (E_COLUMN_READ). Use an ordinary public key
for structure, or a separate entity with its own lifecycle.

### Hops, operators and read through
Write rules and `after insert` keys allow three live hops: `.reaction.message.conversation`, including `exists members[.message.conversation, viewer]`. `messages[id = .message].conversation` is equivalent. Every target must be live and readable; absent, expired or hidden targets remain unknown under `not` and `= null`. Program lookups (`t[id] !`, `exists`) are reads too: a row the caller cannot read is null in an optional lookup (false for program `exists`) and the authored CODE in an asserted lookup, before any later `require` or the delete/update rule runs, so give a moderator read access to what they moderate, or delete by id without a lookup and let the delete rule decide (`guide refusals` has the recipe). `check` notes N_UNREADABLE_PROBE on guards without proved read authority; use unique/cap/after insert constraints for global absence across hidden rows.
Each occurrence prepays one probe, including skipped branches. `check --cost`/`why` list them; prediction needs every read covered.
Insert uses the new image; an unnamed `update <- R` must hold for both the row before and the row after the write (pair `update <- .owner = viewer` with `immutable owner`); a named `update (old, next)` judges exactly what it names; delete uses its pre-delete image; final obligations resolve at transaction end. Read-through capture/lifetimes stay unchanged. Null guards narrow only the same term and image.
Beyond three hops, private/maintained fields and ephemeral targets refuse E_QUARRY_RULE_HOP with concrete mutation `require` checks. A rule says `=`/`!=` over `.col`, `viewer` and literals, `exists`/`created` probes and `and`/`or`/`not`; it orders (`<`, `>=`) only an insert row's own required int/time/decimal/money columns (`.stars >= 1`; an integer literal beside money is minor units) and `update (old, next)` images of the same types. The clock, arithmetic, helper calls and `else CODE` are E_QUARRY_RULE_OPERATOR: a `require … else CODE` in the mutation (`snapback4 why E_QUARRY_RULE_OPERATOR` prints the table of rule forms).

```quarry
table orgs:
  read <- exists members[.id, viewer]
  insert <- allow
  online only
table members:
  org: orgs
  principal: principal
  unique org, principal
  read <- .principal = viewer
  insert <- created orgs[.org] or exists members[.org, viewer]
  online only
table issues:
  org: orgs
  title: text <= 200
  comments: count comments by issue
  immutable org
  read through .org
  insert <- allow
  online only
table comments:
  issue: issues
  author: principal
  body: text <= 2000
  immutable issue
  read through .issue
  insert <- .author = viewer
  delete <- .author = viewer
  online only
query discussion(issue: issues, c: cursor ?):
  comments where .issue = issue first 20 by .id after c
```

### A child inherits its parent's readers
A child names one required immutable reference, without a default, to an ordinary application table. `read through` is its whole read rule; put service grants on the parent. The parent's read-rule fields and authored expiry must be immutable. An insert also needs a live parent readable by the writer, before the child's insert rule runs. The engine captures those inputs; they travel with sync images but never appear in query rows or accept payload values.

Each child expires no later than its parent, through any number of levels. A parent's delete needs read authority and waits until its children are deleted and expired children swept. Its id cannot be reused while physical children remain. A mutable child deadline can shorten its life but cannot extend it past the parent.

`sync` infers exactly the parent's substituted audience after service grants are removed. A conjunction such as membership and an archived flag stays `online only`; `check --verbose` explains its server reads. A parent-pinned page resolves authorization once, while completeness still requires the child's own coverage. An unknown or mismatched parent takes the server fallback. Retained history stays marked `retained: true` beside the server's current page. On these syncing delivered-history children, `retained` is row metadata; name an application column `wasRetained` instead. Row shapes and spreads preserve the mark.

The installed wrapper runs project warnings before the first ordinary check

One material issue in [§10’s upgrade contract](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-b20-dx5/llp/3000.000.000.001-staging-with-real-users.rfc.md:385):

**Old quiet upgrades can suppress warnings and falsely acknowledge delivery.** Both the 0.4.33 and 0.4.35 source snapshots capture the newly installed wrapper’s check output, then discard stderr when `--quiet` is set and check succeeds. The behavior remains visible in [upgrade.js](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-b20-dx5/snapback4/packages/snapback4/bin/upgrade.js:181).

Consequently, an old `upgrade --quiet` or `upgrade --json --quiet` can install the new package, run its wrapper, silently discard the migration warning, and leave a new warning receipt suppressing it on subsequent checks. Fresh-process resolution selects the correct bytes but does not solve delivery.

The amendment needs either a concrete delivery mechanism that survives the old helper’s capture, or an explicit deferred-delivery contract that leaves these warnings unacknowledged until a later check can deliver them. Qualification should cover both quiet combinations from both old versions and verify subsequent warning/receipt behavior.

I found no other material design blocker in the existence-oracle boundary, clock semantics, ReadState, Expo package-resolution requirements, or proof scaffold truthfulness.

This was a read-only semantic review. I inspected historical release-source snapshots; I did not execute published-package upgrades or implementation qualification, and do not count their absence as a finding.
